scope: Current level-60 DPS and tank scenarios, plus conditional spell, item and encounter coverage. This register consolidates the recorded questions; it is not a claim that unlisted game behavior has been verified.
coverage: Read the legacy in-game checks, dispositions, demo checklist, all eleven class/shared/consumable beta-pass reports, mechanics/history/MythicSim/weekly/latest-upstream reviews and tank report. Screened the other top-level source, gear, race, Tier, haste, spell-inventory and patch reports for unresolved claims.

Reviewed 137 spell-manifest records selected for assumed, unreviewed or uncertainty-bearing notes. A manifest label is provenance, not proof of an active bug: stale labels such as Bloodthrill's borrowed ID and Quick Strikes being absent are superseded by current code.

Screened 267 matching runtime comment lines. Unknown-enum names, implementation-language assumptions and unrelated Classic/legacy encounter TODOs are not gameplay questions. Real-item proc/guardian notes remain source-indexed conditional work under DATA-006 and DATA-007.

Generated historical build tables are not independent sources. Their current caveats are represented by class entries; old result counts, paid-hit conventions and unreplayed research are not relabeled as current evidence.

Private chat and combat-log identifiers remain local. Public source links and the committed review conclusions provide the shareable evidence trail. This is consolidation and current-code reconciliation, not a fresh in-game verification of every mechanic.

items.title: Server downranking penalties
items.question: Does the server apply additional low-rank SP penalties beyond client coefficients?
items.current_model: Uses each captured rank coefficient; no unobserved level-60 penalty is invented.
items.impact: Current rank-2 Smite/Lightning Bolt, lower-rank Paladin choices and conditional Frostfire research.

review.answer: Rank coefficients are readable in the client and already used by the engine. The current Forever downranking calculator independently reads build 70009 and likewise warns that hidden server penalties are unconfirmed. Tooltip-based online claims do not measure that missing server term.
review.remaining: Whether an additional penalty depends on player level versus the spell's learned level; especially the level-60 use of very low ranks.
review.implementation: Retain captured coefficients, not an imported Classic/TBC penalty. This remains material to low-rank fillers even after their base damage and costs are sourced.

tests.requires: Two learned ranks of a caster damage spell, controlled SP-only gear changes, fixed target level/resistance and no changing damage talents.
tests.measure: Compare the damage slope per SP at each rank, not their raw hit sizes. Record exact player level and exclude crits; repeat after leveling if possible.

tests.requires: The same spell/rank and controls at level 30.
tests.measure: Check whether its SP slope changes as the player outlevels the rank. This extends the low-level test, not the level-60 conclusion.

tests.requires: Level 60 and the actual downranked spells used by the retained APLs.
tests.measure: Repeat the two-SP slope comparison for low and maximum ranks; separate learned-level base growth from the coefficient.

items.title: Projected gear budget and stat prices
items.question: How representative is equal modeled item cost across physical, caster and tank stats?
items.current_model: Hypothetical level-65 items use sourced quantity/armor/weapon tables but assumed nonlinear allocation budgets and special-stat prices. Equal cost is not equal DPS, and Intellect is not generic SP.
items.impact: All cross-class rankings and gear scaling; tank defensive coverage must not be fabricated.

review.answer: The gear-generation proof reproduces the captured armor/weapon quantity tables, but the allocation exponent, stat prices, Stamina shares and passive-trinket budget are explicit modeling choices. Equal modeled cost is not evidence of equal real-world gearing opportunity or equal DPS. Current requests contain projected equipment, not hidden real-item procs or a paid-hit conversion.
review.remaining: Representativeness of the chosen budget and templates, not an unknown combat mechanic.
review.implementation: Keep the spreadsheet, per-item allocation proofs and legal armor constraints visible. Assess alternative prices as separate scenarios; replace assumptions only when enough current item observations constrain them.

tests.requires: A proposed alternative budget or additional sourced crafted/PvP items.
tests.measure: Fit out-of-sample items and compare total selected stat budgets by role; do not judge equivalence from the final DPS ranking.

items.title: Unresolved real-item stats and acquisition
items.question: Which real catalog entries lack authoritative stats, weapon ranges or legal source/race mapping?
items.current_model: Unresolved records and unavailable old-raid/token sources are excluded from eligible selection. Current rankings use modeled items instead.
items.impact: Manual real-gear use and a future actual-loot benchmark.

review.answer: Unresolved real catalog records are not equipped in the current projected-item benchmark. They cannot explain its damage, threat or survival. Acquisition and stat completeness remain real requirements for enabling those records in a real-gear scenario.
review.remaining: A catalog-import backlog, not a mandatory current-beta combat experiment.
review.implementation: Keep unresolved records excluded and preserve vendor-overlap precedence. Reopen individual records when a real-gear scenario needs them rather than treating the whole catalog as a current mechanics blocker.

tests.requires: Current vendor exports, acquisition records and item/effect tables for a specific excluded item.
tests.measure: Resolve stats, weapon range, availability and unique/faction restrictions independently before making it selectable.

items.title: Ordinary equipped-set proc coverage
items.question: Which disabled set thresholds have enough evidence to implement?
items.current_model: Confirmed passive stat thresholds apply at actual piece counts; 44 unsupported thresholds remain omitted. Legacy handlers do not automatically enable catalog effects.
items.impact: Manual real-item sets; synthetic ranking gear has no ordinary set bonuses.

review.answer: Current projected items have no ordinary set membership. The unsupported ordinary thresholds are intentionally blocked, while supported passive thresholds use actual equipped piece counts. These omitted procs do not affect the forced role Tier 1 scenario, which is a separate mechanism.
review.remaining: Per-threshold implementation work if ordinary real sets are enabled.
review.implementation: Do not enable a legacy handler merely because a set name matches. Maintain threshold-level supported/unsupported records and leave the forced Tier override independent.

tests.requires: A specific ordinary set selected for support and its complete effect/trigger chain.
tests.measure: Separate sourced passive amounts from unknown proc conditions, then check exact piece counts and duplicate suppression.

items.title: Nature's Bounty proc rate and form restrictions
items.question: Is the retained 2% fallback rate correct, and are triggers restricted by active form?
items.current_model: Legacy fallback has separate resource/event routes and Energy ticks over five seconds. Its 2% rate is assumed; catalog proc thresholds remain disabled.
items.impact: Conditional dungeon-set resource behavior, not synthetic rankings.

review.answer: Nature's Bounty is not equipped or activated by the current synthetic loadouts. The retained fallback's 2% rate is an assumption, and checking whether a Druid has a resource bar does not establish an active-form restriction. Neither is evidence of the live set's behavior.
review.remaining: A dormant real-set handler; probability and form routing are unresolved if this set is brought into scope.
review.implementation: Keep its catalog proc threshold disabled. Resource tick timing already has client support and need not be conflated with the unknown chance.

items.title: Legacy item and enchant proc assumptions
items.question: Which inherited handlers still use assumed PPM, triggers or obsolete effect values?
items.current_model: Numerous real-item handlers retain explicit assumptions; some source-supported amount updates are known but not imported. Synthetic weapons/trinkets have no implicit item procs, but their selected enchants can supply proc effects.
items.impact: Manual catalog items and proc enchants on the projected gear pool. Form-specific enchant eligibility is tracked separately.

review.answer: This is material even with synthetic weapons: current requests equip 120 Crusader enchant copies and 28 Fiery copies. Crusader's client spell explicitly contains a 75–125 self-heal alongside 100 Strength for 15 seconds, but the handler implements only Strength. Its unbounded below-60 formula also grants more than 100 Strength at lower levels. Fiery's 40 base damage is sourced; its 6 PPM and Crusader's 1 PPM are not established by those effect amounts.
review.remaining: Effective proc frequency, special/extra-attack eligibility, form handling and healing resolution/threat. Legacy real-item amount updates remain a separate dormant catalog backlog.
review.implementation: Add the sourced Crusader heal and correct the below-60 Strength arithmetic with targeted regressions before a later affected tank refresh. Lifestealing's health-leech effect is also reduced to damage-only, but no current profile equips it. Do not interpret a proc wrapper's 100% field as a 100%-per-swing rate.

tests.requires: Crusader enchant 1900 → spell 20007; fixed proc events at levels 20 and 60.
tests.measure: Check 100 Strength, the sourced self-heal range, health capping and damage/threat separation. Verify Lifestealing's heal separately if that enchant is enabled.

tests.requires: Actual Crusader/Fiery enchants, fixed-speed weapons and separate white-only, special-attack and extra-swing samples. Move earlier only if the beta supplies these high-skill enchants.
tests.measure: Estimate probability by eligible event type and weapon speed; record haste, handedness and form. A triggered spell's coefficient does not establish its PPM.

review.code_ready: Add Crusader's sourced self-heal and stop the Strength formula increasing below level 60; leave PPM and proc eligibility separately qualified.

items.title: Item guardian stats and attacks
items.question: What are the actual stats, attacks and resource limits of item-summoned guardians?
items.current_model: Eskhandar, Core Hound and Emerald Whelp retain approximate inherited stats/timing. Dragon's Call's flat-damage upstream change was not blindly imported.
items.impact: Optional real-item use; absent from projected equipment.

review.answer: Eskhandar, the item Core Hound and Dragon's Call Whelp are not summoned by the current fixed-stat projected gear. Their approximate stats cannot affect this benchmark. This does not close the separate, active Summon Hawk talent question.
review.remaining: Item-specific guardian research if the corresponding real items become legal selected candidates.
review.implementation: Do not merge item guardians with Hunter/Warlock pets or infer all guardians from one summon.

items.title: Unimplemented vendor item effects
items.question: What prevents Adaptive Combat Assistant, Defender's Grip Stabilizer and Totem of the Storm from being used?
items.current_model: Absorb/explosion, location-dependent modifier and Maelstrom-related proc are excluded rather than supplied as free stats/effects.
items.impact: Future real-item choices; no current modeled-item effect.

review.answer: The client supplies more than placeholder names. Adaptive Combat Assistant has a 450-point, 15-second all-school absorb and a separate 90–110 Nature explosion. Defender's Grip Stabilizer grants 8% Block for 15 seconds, doubled in Strongholds/Cities; its ordinary outside-city branch is source-ready. Totem of the Storm says Lightning Bolt can trigger Maelstrom at a 50% reduced chance. All three remain absent from the current synthetic equipment.
review.remaining: Assistant's early-removal/depletion trigger and Totem's effective spell proc probability; explicit location handling if city/Stronghold scenarios are introduced.
review.implementation: Defender's ordinary raid branch does not need a future game test before implementation. Assistant first needs the finite absorb infrastructure. Do not give the Totem a free stat bonus or invent a spell-normalization denominator from its dummy aura.

tests.measure: Implement only explicitly supported branches, preserving item cooldowns and shared use categories.

tests.requires: Level-60 vendor items; controlled damage into Assistant, and Maelstrom-talented Shaman with the Totem.
tests.measure: Separate shield depletion, normal expiry and dispel; count explosion events. For Totem, compare Lightning Bolt proc rate with independently measured melee eligibility, holding talent rank fixed.

review.code_ready: Implement Defender's Grip's ordinary outside-city 8% Block for 15 seconds; do not invent the other items' script behavior.

items.title: Raw haste rating conversion
items.question: Can future raw haste-rating items be represented without confusing ratings and flat percentages?
items.current_model: Current item/enchant representation handles sourced flat effects; the inherited raw-rating constant is not certified for new Forever rating-bearing items.
items.impact: Future item ingestion and hypothetical gear sensitivity; no selected raw haste-rating item.

review.answer: The captured level-60 combat table explicitly gives 10 raw haste rating per percent. The missing work is representing raw rating separately from flat percentages throughout import/UI/engine, not discovering that conversion in game. The current synthetic pool does not add a new raw-haste-rating stat.
review.remaining: A typed data/engine migration before raw rating-bearing equipment is supported.
review.implementation: Preserve general haste versus attack/cast-speed-only scopes and test one conversion at the boundary. Do not divide existing flat-percent enchants by ten.

tests.requires: Separate raw-rating and flat-percent fixtures at level 60.
tests.measure: Ten raw rating must yield 1%; an explicit 1% effect must remain 1%. Check native, web and export/import paths and their affected timers.

review.code_ready: Represent raw haste rating separately from flat percentages, using the sourced level-60 conversion of 10 rating per percent.

items.title: Item-picker shared-crit EP
items.question: Does the gear picker value generic crit for casters the way the engine does?
items.current_model: Engine sharing works, but the picker can dot-product the unprojected MeleeCrit field against zero caster weight. This is a display/valuation limitation, not missing simulated crit.
items.impact: Manual item sorting; native coordinate simulations are not driven by that displayed EP.

review.answer: The picker still directly dot-products the stored item stats against EP weights. The engine first shares equipment crit/hit between physical and spell fields. A caster with zero MeleeCrit weight therefore can undervalue an item whose generic crit is stored there. This is a reproducible valuation mismatch, not missing caster crit in combat.
review.remaining: Picker valuation/cache alignment with the actual equipment projection, including enchants and random suffixes.
review.implementation: Use the same shared-stat semantics once and retain scope-specific exceptions such as ranged scopes. Simulator-driven gear searches are not using this picker EP as their DPS result.

tests.requires: Generic-crit equipment with only a SpellCrit EP weight, plus ranged-only scope control.
tests.measure: Compare predicted picker deltas to the projected equipment stats. Check that sharing is neither omitted nor applied twice.

review.code_ready: Project shared equipment crit/hit into picker valuation exactly once, preserving explicitly scoped exceptions.

items.title: Explicitly scoped crit items
items.question: Are any remaining catalog items incorrectly treated as generic crit despite a scoped effect?
items.current_model: Generic equipment fields are shared; checked current flat-crit loadouts had no contradictory scoped record. That does not certify every legacy proc/enchant.
items.impact: Unreviewed manual gear choices.

review.answer: The active scoped exception is already explicit: SAF-T enchant 8720 routes spell 1310308's bow/gun/crossbow-restricted 2% crit to ranged attacks, rather than generic equipment crit. Current projected items use intentionally generic stat fields. The earlier real-item audit is not evidence for every future proc, but no unresolved generic/scoped contradiction was found in these current flat-stat loadouts.
review.remaining: Reopen only for a particular imported effect with a contradictory mask; legacy proc coverage stays under DATA-006.
review.implementation: No broad crit rewrite is warranted. Fix the separate picker projection without widening ability, talent, school or ranged-only bonuses.

items.title: Spell acquisition and source-scanner coverage
items.question: Which retained records are learnable abilities rather than NPC, rune, teaching or obsolete aliases?
items.current_model: Class skill lines supplement class masks; runtime registration and static source coverage are separate. Lower ranks and unresolved generic registration sites are disclosed.
items.impact: Prevents missing real abilities or enabling unavailable ones.
legacy: T50 in check_dispositions.md (acquisition watch) / T05 / H30

review.answer: The stored inventory distinguishes 151 candidate families: 91 registered, 12 aliases, 10 conditional, 18 not used, six unimplemented, eight awaiting pet data and six awaiting acquisition. It is a historical sampled-runtime inventory, not proof that every current rank/tank/talent path is covered. Several dispositions are stale: current tanks register shield/Bear abilities, and Wrack has since entered the Affliction profile. Felfire is an unproven Mage record, not a missing Warlock spell.
review.remaining: Refresh the coverage census for current supported contexts and preserve acquisition holds for Black Arrow, active Hunter Lacerate, Felfire, Lava Breath, Hammer of the Righteous and Victory Rush. Their names/class association alone do not authorize implementation.
review.implementation: Update runtime sampling and per-family dispositions separately from static source-ID coverage. Keep real missing abilities, teaching aliases and inactive talent paths distinct. Victory Rush also lacks a qualifying kill in the current encounter.

tests.requires: Current SkillLineAbility/trait/teaching records plus legal runtime contexts for each supported class, tank and selectable pet.
tests.measure: Reconcile each learned rank and alias against registration; do not treat a source-code number match as full ability coverage. Seek an actual acquisition chain before promoting held records.

items.title: Talent-tree source conflicts
items.question: Which old client/crawl disagreements still affect the legal tree rather than only historical metadata?
items.current_model: Current selectable trees use the later client-backed removals, rank curves and September 24 official position changes. Retired video-extraction JSON and earlier audit verdicts are not the active tree.
items.impact: Future tree updates and under-reviewed rank values.

review.answer: The September 17 audit contains a later reversal that supersedes its earlier rejection: the crawl was old BlizzCon material, not an independent reading of that beta. The live UI trees already remove Balance of Nature/Vitality, use Flawless Execution/Wrack, remove Aggression's old prerequisite and use the revised Shaman layout. Moonglow 8/17/25, Moonfury 2/4/6/8/10, Lethality 4/8/12/16/20 and Stings 6/13/20 are already in UI and engine. September 24's official Focused Rage/Bastion swap supersedes the older positions still present in the captured node table.
review.remaining: The retired video-extraction trees and old audit sections are historical inputs, not current selectable defaults. Individual newly found effect-scope questions remain under their class IDs.
review.implementation: Close the stale conflict list; preserve its reversal and raw-table/version distinction. Do not regenerate current trees from the older extraction JSON or blindly restore the pre-patch node coordinates.

items.title: Tank boss damage and external healing
items.question: What incoming damage and healing should define a representative tank comparison?
items.current_model: Explicit stress scenarios: one 300-second boss or three 90-second attackers with fixed swing/AP/armor/healing settings. These are not observed raid bosses or healer behavior.
items.impact: Tank DPS, rage, mana, threat and death rates; cannot be silently equated with un-attacked DPS rows.

review.answer: The incoming-damage and healing values are explicit controlled workloads, not claims about a known raid boss. The single workload is 300 seconds with one 3000-base/2-second attacker and 1500 external HPS; the multi workload is 90 seconds with three 1500-base/2-second attackers and 2500 HPS. There is no unique game-mechanics experiment that can prove these are the representative encounter.
review.remaining: Which workloads are useful comparisons, and future measured encounter inputs.
review.implementation: Keep exact requests and per-target threat/survival outputs. Older tables in the original tank document describe superseded models; current request artifacts are authoritative.

tests.requires: A chosen workload or credible raid-log encounter specification.
tests.measure: Change damage/healing assumptions as a separately labeled scenario and compare matched inputs, rather than silently redefining the tank benchmark.

items.title: Non-tank external healing abstraction
items.question: How should health costs constrain Life Tap, Death and self-damaging consumables in DPS scenarios?
items.current_model: Self-damage is excluded from enemy DPS. Non-tanking resource use retains its external-healing abstraction rather than a finite healer budget; tank requests pay real health costs.
items.impact: Resource sustainability and practical healer burden.

review.answer: Non-tanking Life Tap deliberately does not debit health; tanking Life Tap pays the sourced health cost. Death and consumable self-hits are excluded from enemy DPS, while health depletion follows the core's configured survival model. The non-tank benchmark therefore assumes health support; it does not establish sustainable healer burden or survival.
review.remaining: Whether to add a finite-healing DPS scenario, not whether self-damage should be counted as boss damage.
review.implementation: Expose the health-support abstraction and preserve self-damage accounting. A constrained healer budget would be a new scenario and could alter resource-limited rotations.

tests.requires: An explicit incoming-damage/healer-resource model and failure condition for non-tanks.
tests.measure: Compare paid health, effective healing, overheal and deaths separately from outgoing enemy damage.

items.title: Tank target selection and threat coverage
items.question: Can a tank maintain threat on the weakest-covered enemy rather than repeatedly attacking the first?
items.current_model: Existing Warrior multi-target presets remain single-target focused; summed TPS masks very low threat on an add. No lowest-threat target selector is provided.
items.impact: First-class AoE tank support and meaningful optimization.

review.answer: This is an APL capability gap, not unknown game behavior. The available unit references do not provide a lowest-threat target selector. Saved multi-target tank results demonstrate why total TPS cannot substitute for the weakest add's threat.
review.remaining: Explicit target selection/cycling with target-local debuffs and threat coverage.
review.implementation: Define a selector policy and use target-specific state; preserve self-maintained Sunder on the intended target. Do not infer raid aggro control solely from one player's total threat.

tests.requires: A three-target fixture with deliberately unequal per-target threat and debuff durations.
tests.measure: Check selection, switching, maintenance and minimum target TPS; ensure current-target lookups do not accidentally read the first target's aura.

items.title: Tank selection after correctness and support corrections
items.question: Has tank gear/talent selection been repeated under the corrected queue model and common support?
items.current_model: All 17 tanks have common raid support and fresh matched replays with fixed equipment/talents. Protection Warrior’s earlier direct-cast search is invalid. Other historical selection gains describe superseded class-specific support, not a current optimum.
items.impact: Protection selection quality is not established by the superseded search. Corrected damage/threat results are not a new optimization claim.

review.answer: No new complete gear/talent selection was performed after the queue and shared-support corrections. Current tank results are fixed-loadout correctness replays; the invalid direct-cast Warrior search and unequal-support selection controls remain superseded. This is known workflow scope, not an unanswered game mechanic.
review.remaining: A separately scoped tank-selection campaign under current mechanics, if requested.
review.implementation: Do not call fixed corrected loadouts an optimum. Future selection must use current support, legal queued attacks, both workloads and disjoint confirmation ranges.

tests.requires: An authorized selection pass with current frozen controls and survival/threat constraints.
tests.measure: Retain only validated gains under corrected mechanics; do not compare against historical invalid controls.

items.title: General absorb-pool and shielding threat
items.question: Do generic shields consume finite incoming damage and generate correct threat?
items.current_model: The generic Shield helper records shielding without a full pool-consumption model or shielding threat. Templar's Bulwark has its own finite pool and is no longer the old 99% reduction shortcut.
items.impact: Priest/healing shields and future Seal of Fury integration; not a reason to revert correct Bulwark behavior.

review.answer: The generic Shield helper really does only activate an aura and record generated shielding; it has no remaining-capacity consumption path and sets threat to zero as a TODO. Bulwark independently has a finite health-sized pool. Implementing the generic pool is source/code work, while effective shielding threat and interactions need their own evidence.
review.remaining: Generic absorption, expiry and ordering; sourced threat on application versus absorption. Current tanks do not acquire a generic external shield from the existing healing model.
review.implementation: Reuse an explicit finite-pool model rather than treating generated shielding as effective mitigation. Keep generated, consumed and expired shielding distinct; preserve Bulwark's existing behavior.

tests.requires: A shield with a sourced amount/duration and sequential controlled incoming hits.
tests.measure: Verify partial and full consumption, expiry, overwrites and ordering without converting unconsumed capacity into effective healing.

tests.requires: Priest with Power Word: Shield, a cooperating player and a controlled hostile target with threat observation.
tests.measure: Separate threat on shield application, actual absorption and unused expiry; do not attribute incidental healing or damage threat to the shield.

review.code_ready: Implement generic remaining absorb capacity separately from generated shielding; keep the unknown threat rule separate and preserve Bulwark.

items.title: In-range and reactive damage omissions
items.question: Which supported damage actions remain missing outside the stationary reference rotation?
items.current_model: Hellfire and Humanoid-only Chastise remain absent; Mage Cone of Cold/Frost Nova are now implemented. Several parry, mana-burn and reactive actions lack encounter support.
items.impact: AoE, solo and alternate target types, not proof of a current five-minute gain.

review.answer: Hellfire and Chastise are specific supported missing damage families, not evidence that all unregistered database records are player spells. Chastise's Humanoid-only restriction prevents use on the Dragonkin reference target. Hellfire requires a different range/AoE scenario than the current 20-yard Warlock profiles. Mage area spells are already present.
review.remaining: Optional in-range/appropriate-target implementations and refreshed inventory dispositions; current simulated tank mitigation must not be inferred from absent reactive utility.
review.implementation: Implement sourced ranks, costs, channels and restrictions when their scenario is supported. Leave unproven acquisition records under DATA-013 rather than adopting them as missing abilities.

tests.requires: Current Hellfire/Chastise effect chains and explicit in-range or Humanoid targets.
tests.measure: Verify enemy versus self-damage, rank availability, target restrictions and range; the present Dragonkin/20-yard controls must not gain free damage.

items.title: Forced Tier 1 and synthetic stat scaling
items.question: What do the Tier-off and +10%/+50% scenarios establish?
items.current_model: Full role Tier 1 is forced independently of equipment. Stat/weapon scaling holds enchants/procs/talents/APLs fixed; amplification is finite-range curvature, not proof of exponential growth or future loot.
items.impact: Interpretation of all matrix gain columns.

review.answer: The three sensitivity scenarios already have a precise mathematical interpretation. Tier-off removes the role override, and +10%/+50% multiply item stats and weapon damage while keeping other inputs fixed. Amplification divides the equal-race-weight +50% gain by five times the +10% gain; it rejects negligible/noisy/nonpositive denominators. This measures finite-range curvature, not isolated synergy or exponential growth.
review.remaining: These controlled scenarios do not forecast future loot mixtures, cap changes, proc gear or reoptimized rotations.
review.implementation: Retain paired requests and hash-checked baseline association. A new gearing distribution is a new scenario, not a reinterpretation of the current column.

items.title: Windfury Totem in animal forms
items.question: Does the redesigned party buff proc for Cat and Bear?
items.current_model: Cat/form eligibility is provisionally enabled under the separate party-buff model; the removed weapon-imbue restriction is not conclusive proof.
items.impact: Feral and Bear damage, rage and proc interactions.

review.answer: The redesigned Totem is a party buff rather than a weapon imbue, so the removed weapon-application restriction no longer proves form exclusion. It also does not prove form eligibility. No direct Forever form-proc measurement was found in the reviewed public evidence.
review.remaining: Cat/Bear eligibility and extra-swing outcomes under the current party buff.
review.implementation: Keep the current allowed-form treatment explicitly provisional and separate from Crusader form eligibility.

tests.requires: A Shaman with Windfury Totem (level 32), grouped Cat/Bear and no Grace of Air. Earlier only if the beta grants that buff explicitly.
tests.measure: Record buff presence and isolated auto/extra-attack events in each form; use a humanoid weapon-attack control. The Druid reaching level 20 alone is insufficient access.

items.title: Other omitted mitigation and threat effects
items.question: Which acknowledged non-DPS effects become relevant with incoming attacks?
items.current_model: Hurricane's attack slow, some pet utility mitigation, Counterspell/Feint threat, general taunt/target switching and legacy encounter behaviors are not a complete tank/raid model.
items.impact: Conditional tank/raid/solo scenarios; not universal current benchmark damage errors.

review.answer: This catch-all mixes optional encounter support with already separately tracked effects. The stationary benchmarks have no interruptible casts, taunt swaps or moving enemies. Counterspell/Feint control behavior is therefore not a blocking uncertainty for them. Pet Screech's omitted AP reduction is a specific sourced implementation gap under HUN-009, not something to lose inside this umbrella.
review.remaining: Utility encounter support when those actors and events are introduced; exact current threat/accounting defects remain active under narrower IDs.
review.implementation: Use explicit per-effect tasks instead of a permanent 'tank completeness' question. Hurricane slow requires a channeling Druid in range; it is not a free raid debuff.

items.title: Power Infusion on another raid member
items.question: Can an owned Priest cast Power Infusion on a selected other player?
items.current_model: The owned ability lacks a general target-player option; external buff settings are a separate abstraction.
items.impact: Multi-player raid support and support-DPS comparisons.

review.answer: The owned Priest spell explicitly constructs Power Infusion on its own Unit and ignores the target-player option. External PI is a different abstraction. There is no missing probability or hidden coefficient preventing a target-selection implementation.
review.remaining: Native/web target plumbing and provider ownership.
review.implementation: Retain the Priest's mana cost/cooldown while applying the aura to the selected valid friendly player. Prevent overlap with independently configured external coverage.

tests.requires: A two-player raid, self/other/invalid target options and external PI controls.
tests.measure: Verify who pays the cost, who receives the aura, cooldown ownership, targeting fallback and duplicate prevention.

review.code_ready: Wire owned Power Infusion to the selected friendly player while keeping cost and cooldown on the Priest.

items.title: Legacy regression-suite alignment
items.question: Can the full inherited test suite run against the current Forever data and presets, beyond the maintained release checks?
items.current_model: The release runs targeted mechanics, source-coverage, tank and browser tests. The broader suite still includes excluded Classic items, pre-patch talent metadata, obsolete tree/proto-layout expectations and old landing-page assumptions.
items.impact: Automated regression coverage; a failing legacy fixture is not itself evidence that current game calculations are wrong.

review.answer: A focused rerun reproduced five failing inherited checks: old 69893 talent values, contiguous proto-number assumptions, stale exported presets, and two obsolete landing-page contracts. The slot-collision check passed. One production metadata constant also remains stale: Paladin's final tree size is 18 although the current tree has 17 entries. This last-tree size does not shift the current valid strings, but it should be corrected rather than dismissing every failure as a fixture issue.
review.remaining: Fixture/preset/metadata cleanup and a documented full-suite contract, separate from environment/toolchain failures.
review.implementation: Update the retained Paladin size and obsolete preset exports, and migrate assertions to declaration-order fields/current sources. Elemental's invalid legacy Level 60 export is not the BuildPresets list actually used by its current picker. Do not revert source-backed post-patch values to satisfy old expectations.

tests.requires: Current generated databases, known toolchain and the inherited tests outside the release allowlist.
tests.measure: Classify each failing assertion as stale fixture, real defect or environment problem before broadening the release gate.

review.code_ready: Correct the stale final Paladin tree-size constant and obsolete exports; update old assertions without reverting current sourced mechanics.

items.title: Unequal tank raid support
items.question: Do tank defaults provide consistent raid support and supported weapon consumables?
items.current_model: A shared native/web support definition covers all 17 tank profiles, preserving explicitly self-maintained duties. Paladin has Brilliant Wizard Oil and Curse of Elements; Titans remains the main tank flask.
items.impact: The old Paladin preset omitted substantial damage support. Comparisons now use the corrected settings without claiming that all class survival mechanics are verified.

review.answer: The shared support definition and all 17 tank profiles contain the intended common support, preserving self-maintained duties. Paladin's supported oil and primary Titans flask are present. This question is closed; overlapping historical confirmations concern statistical independence, not whether those request fields exist.
review.remaining: No new tank-support discrepancy identified here. DPS Improved Imp/Blood Pact is a separate issue and not selected by these tanks.
review.implementation: Retain exact support/default regressions; do not reopen solved request plumbing because a different mechanic remains uncertain.

items.title: Overlapping seeds in historical validation
items.question: Which earlier pooled comparisons counted overlapping iteration seeds as independent replications?
items.current_model: The engine uses starting seed plus iteration index. The preceding tank-support and queue reports used starts 38 and 52 apart for 10,000 iterations, reusing most seeds. New Sunder validation uses disjoint ranges.
items.impact: Legacy pooled sample-size and uncertainty claims need reassessment; this does not by itself invalidate saved DPS means or change combat behavior.

review.answer: The overlap extends beyond the two known tank reports. Current modeled-gear confirmation uses starts one apart for 5,000 iterations: 5,001 distinct iteration seeds, not 10,000. Research-build confirmation has 5,060 distinct seeds; Paladin mana confirmation has 100,046 rather than 200,000. Several historical tank selection cohorts similarly overlap. The latest Sunder confirmation is genuinely disjoint, including its 25,000-iteration Orc extension.
review.remaining: Correct older independence claims/uncertainty estimates and use nonoverlapping seed ranges for future selection confirmations.
review.implementation: Guard full [seed, seed+iterations-1] intervals, not just unequal starting seeds. validate_gear.py currently accepts unequal starts and then combines their SEs as independent. Preserve original results; repeated means are not automatically false gains, but the stated independent-replication confidence is unsupported. Current single-seed benchmark rows and deliberately paired baseline/Tier comparisons are not the same error.

tests.requires: Saved requests/iteration counts and the explicit seed-range inventory.
tests.measure: Reject overlap within claimed independent replications. Recalculate uncertainty from unique iterations where available, or repeat only material decisions with disjoint ranges; do not rewrite archived raw evidence.

review.code_ready: Reject intersecting iteration-seed ranges in independent confirmations and qualify old independence-based uncertainty claims.

items.title: Healing is not inferred spell damage
items.question: Are pure healing effects accidentally converted to spell damage?
items.current_model: The generic one-third fallback is removed. Sourced hybrid healing/damage effects are imported separately, including enchants.
items.impact: Historical gear/enchant misvaluation; current projected catalogs and real-effect imports retain explicit values.

review.answer: The generic healing-to-damage fallback is absent from current equipment compilation. Hybrid healing/damage effects retain separate sourced values, including enchants and supported set effects.

items.title: Hot Streak and Clearcasting consumption
items.question: Can the old persistent proc buffs still provide repeated accelerated/free casts?
items.current_model: Completed Pyroblast consumes Hot Streak; eligible paid damage casts consume Clearcasting using underlying cost, not the discounted zero.

review.answer: Hot Streak is consumed by completed Pyroblast and Clearcasting consumption checks underlying paid cost. The old permanent-proc defects are not present in current code.
review.remaining: Proc ordering and in-flight edge cases are narrower MAG-004/MAG-005 questions, not the same fixed bug.
review.implementation: Keep the existing consumption regressions; do not preserve Hot Streak indefinitely to increase Fire damage.

items.title: Death, Early Demise and Penance timing
items.question: Are these Priest abilities/talents still missing or using evenly spaced Penance bolts?
items.current_model: Four learned Death ranks and Early Demise are registered. Penance hits at 0/1/2 seconds before channel modifiers, not 0.667/1.333/2.

review.answer: All four learned Death ranks and Early Demise are registered. Penance has an immediate first bolt and two subsequent one-second intervals before its channel modifiers; the timing regression covers the immediate bolt.

review.implementation: Do not reopen the missing-spell or evenly-spaced-Penance defects.

items.title: Mage Armor, Innervate accounting and timing
items.question: Are Mage Armor and apparent negative Innervate returns still broken?
items.current_model: Current Mage profiles use available Mage Armor. Innervate bonus regeneration has its own accounting; optional external Innervate waits for enough missing mana rather than firing at a fixed 85%.
items.impact: Historical mana/reporting issues; the ranked Mages have no external Innervate.

review.answer: Current Mage Armor uses its supported casting-regeneration effect. Innervate's extra regeneration is separately accounted, and its external activation threshold considers expected regeneration/missing mana rather than a fixed 85% gate.
review.remaining: The optional MP5 interpretation and any future source-specific regeneration correction are separate questions.
review.implementation: Preserve the repaired default mode; an assumed fivefold MP5 mode is not required to fix Innervate.

items.title: Shared crit aura, legal imbues and air buffs
items.question: Are Moonkin/Leader and Windfury/Grace still incorrectly stacked?
items.current_model: Moonkin/Leader are one 3% global-crit benefit. Windfury Totem and Grace are exclusive; only Shamans can use Windfury Weapon, and empty/nonweapon slots cannot receive weapon imbues.
items.impact: Confirmed configuration errors corrected; generic crit remains distinct from scoped crit effects.

review.answer: The raid crit auras share one global benefit; incompatible air buffs are exclusive. Windfury Weapon is Shaman-only, and nonweapon/empty slots do not receive weapon imbues. The current checks cover these configuration rules.
review.remaining: Windfury's detailed attack resolution and animal-form eligibility remain separate evidence questions.
review.implementation: No second crit-aura benefit or non-Shaman weapon proc should be reintroduced.

items.title: Legal armor, shield Block and Bulwark
items.question: Can Feral import plate, do shields lack base Block, or is Bulwark unlimited reduction?
items.current_model: Native armor ceilings reject illegal Druid armor; intrinsic shield Block is imported; Shield Block recasts restore charges; Bulwark is a finite eight-second pool and has no GCD.
items.impact: Reproduced tank/import defects are fixed, not remaining gameplay tests.
legacy: W1 / W2 / W4 / W8 / H20 (Bulwark portion)

review.answer: Druid armor ceilings are enforced natively, shield base Block is imported, active Shield Block recasts replenish charges, and Bulwark consumes a finite eight-second pool instead of granting unlimited reduction.
review.remaining: The generic Shield helper and other unimplemented tank effects are separate from these corrected paths.
review.implementation: Preserve armor legality and finite-pool regressions; do not equate the remaining generic-shield gap with a broken Bulwark.

items.title: Life Tap, Moonfury and explicit pet bonuses
items.question: Are the latest source-backed class-effects fixes actually applied?

items.impact: Published fixed-profile correctness release; not pending code changes.

review.remaining: No reversal of these supported corrections; Imp-specific new findings are tracked separately.
review.implementation: Keep the existing class-effect regressions and provider lifecycle checks.

items.title: Demonic Sacrifice coexistence false lead
items.question: Can a no-Pact Warlock keep sacrifice benefits with an active pet?
items.current_model: Pet reset/enable ordering cancels the sacrifice. Full-run checks recorded zero combat aura/mana benefit without Pact.

review.answer: The no-Pact sacrifice coexistence lead was disproved by the full reset/enable sequence and zero combat benefit. Reading only owner Reset was incomplete.
review.remaining: None for that alleged defect.
review.implementation: Keep the retraction and do not add a redundant behavior-changing guard based on the old partial trace.

items.title: Lightning Shield's unsupported Earth Shock reset
items.question: Does recasting Lightning Shield reset Earth Shock?
items.current_model: The inherited personal-timer reset is removed. The shared shock timer had already blocked demonstrated extra casts, so it was not a proven DPS exploit.
items.impact: Correctness cleanup, not an unexplained damage gain.

review.answer: The unsupported Lightning Shield personal-timer reset was removed. The shared shock timer had already prevented a demonstrated extra Earth Shock, so the historical finding is not evidence of a former large DPS exploit.
review.remaining: Normal Maelstrom and shield behavior have separate questions.
review.implementation: Retain the real-cast/shared-cooldown regression and the qualified historical account.

items.title: Seal of Command SP placement comparison
items.question: Does this engine omit the 70% multiplier on personal SP that upstream added?
items.current_model: No: proc DamageMultiplier is 0.7 × Improved Seals × weapon specialization, with BonusCoefficient 0.29. Personal SP passes through that multiplier; target Holy bonus is applied separately afterward.
items.impact: A recent review overstated the difference by comparing field placement rather than final math. Righteousness remains genuinely unresolved.

review.answer: Seal of Command's personal SP contribution already passes through its 0.7 damage multiplier. The upstream placement change therefore does not establish an omitted multiplier here. Target Holy bonus is a separate later calculation.
review.remaining: Independent seal trigger/scaling questions do not justify multiplying personal SP by 0.7 twice.
review.implementation: No correction to this traced multiplier-placement claim.

items.title: Cone of Cold, Frost Nova and owned Mana Tide
items.question: Are the later sourced spell additions still absent?
items.current_model: Mage area spells have ranked damage, cooldowns and 10-yard checks. Owned Mana Tide has its real cast, costs, four pulses and water replacement. Control geometry and owned Mana Spring remain separate gaps.
items.impact: Old spell-coverage pages are historical, not evidence these registrations are missing.

review.remaining: Owned Mana Spring and movement/control geometry are distinct gaps.
review.implementation: Do not retain these completed spell additions in the unresolved queue.

items.title: Removed and unavailable effects excluded
items.question: Are old Sanctity, Molten Armor, Cat Mangle, campfire raid buffs or Shaman dual wield still granted?
items.current_model: These unsupported choices are excluded; regular Faerie Fire works in supported forms. Surviving legacy records alone do not enable them.
items.impact: Previous illegal/free-effect setups are not current baseline assumptions.

review.answer: Removed/unavailable choices are excluded from supported defaults and legality checks. Retained legacy records do not make Sanctity, Molten Armor, Cat Mangle, raid campfire effects or Shaman dual wield valid.
review.remaining: A specific current acquisition source is required to reopen an availability exclusion.
review.implementation: Keep exclusions explicit rather than reactivating a spell from its name or old ID.

items.title: Self-damage is not encounter DPS
items.question: Do Demonic Rune and Sapper self-hits inflate outgoing DPS?
items.current_model: Self-hits are excluded from outgoing encounter damage/threat while preserving damage-taken/resource behavior.
items.impact: Historical accounting inflation fixed; health sustainability is a separate scenario assumption.

review.answer: Self-target damage does not contribute to enemy DPS/threat. Demonic Rune and Sapper retain their self-cost/resource behavior under the configured health model.
review.remaining: Finite non-tank healing support is a scenario question, not an unresolved DPS aggregation bug.
review.implementation: Preserve the enemy/self-target accounting regression and the health-support qualification.

items.title: Hunter trigger scopes and shared rank cooldowns
items.question: Are Expose Prey and the audited per-rank cooldown bypasses still incorrect?
items.current_model: Expose Prey excludes generic trap spell hits. Audited Paladin/Warlock spell ranks share timers; Holy Shield requires a shield. Hunter cost and Predator's Edge masks have the later source-backed corrections.
items.impact: Earlier trigger, free-cost and rank-bypass findings are implemented corrections, not open proc-rate tests.

review.answer: Expose Prey's current attack mask excludes generic trap spell hits. Audited rank families share cooldown timers, and Holy Shield requires an actual shield. These concrete fixes remain present.
review.remaining: Mongoose's first incoming-dodge listener and unreviewed utility categories remain separate, narrower tasks.
review.implementation: Keep the scoped regressions rather than reopening all Hunter trigger/cooldown behavior.

items.title: Blood Pact talent bonus and pet-provider lifecycle
items.question: Does the current Improved Imp talent still increase Blood Pact, and do owned pet transitions update party buffs?
items.current_model: The engine still supplies an obsolete 30% improved Blood Pact flag, turning 54 Stamina into 70. Automatic party provision also remains static rather than following all pet transitions.
items.impact: Tank health and party simulations involving an Imp.

review.answer: There is a more immediate sourced defect than partial-rank lifecycle handling: current Improved Imp modifies Firebolt and Fire Shield, not Blood Pact. The engine still turns three points into an improved Blood Pact and applies a 30% Stamina multiplier to that external flag. A regression currently asserts 70 instead of the ordinary 54. All 184 saved DPS requests select the improved flag; the 17 tank requests do not select Blood Pact.
review.remaining: Remove the obsolete talent multiplier and improved UI choice under Forever, then implement provider lifecycle independently. There is no new partial-rank Blood Pact bonus to invent.
review.implementation: Preserve Classic separately, the sourced base/rank growth and party scope. Record the current affected health totals before correcting requests; do not silently rerun or relabel benchmark results during this research pass. Summoning/sacrificing/dismissing an Imp must not supply a permanent owned aura.

tests.requires: Forever/Classic fixtures, Improved Imp ranks 0–3, explicit external coverage and owned Imp transitions.
tests.measure: Verify no Forever talent increase to Blood Pact, preserved Classic behavior, correct party-only scope and activation/deactivation without removing an independent external provider.

review.code_ready: Remove Improved Imp's obsolete Forever Blood Pact multiplier and improved UI flag; retain the ordinary sourced buff and Classic behavior.

items.title: Summon Hawk guardian model
items.question: How do Hawk attacks, two-Hawk coexistence and inherited stats actually work?
items.current_model: One periodic guardian surrogate: six ticks at three-second intervals using dive-bomb base values. The opening hit uses 5% RAP; this is not a measured complete guardian formula.
items.impact: Pet/Melee row and Hawk alternatives; major model-dependent build opportunity.

review.answer: The current client explicitly allows two Hawks, supplies a separate summon chain and specifies 5% RAP for the opening dive. One refreshed six-tick DoT cannot represent two independently expiring guardians. The remaining unknown is the sustained guardian attack profile, not whether two summons are permitted.
review.remaining: Sustained attacks, inheritance, crit, target switching and replacement of the oldest guardian.
review.implementation: Separate the sourced opening hit and two guardian lifetimes from the unmeasured sustained formula. Do not present the current surrogate as a complete implementation or substitute the wiki's differently rendered opening numbers for raw rank values.

tests.requires: Level 25+ Hunter with Summon Hawk; fixed target, RAP and pet settings.
tests.measure: Summon once, twice and a third time before expiry. Separate opening damage from each guardian's later events and record despawns. Repeat with different owner RAP/crit without changing the target.

tests.requires: Higher Hawk ranks and the actual role Tier effects.
tests.measure: Verify rank progression and Tier interactions after the low-rank guardian model is established.

items.title: Pet families and new trained abilities
items.question: Which new family abilities can be added with verified learning paths and effects?
items.current_model: Claw, Bite, Lightning Breath, Screech and Scorpid Poison are supported, not every new teaching record. Wolf Howl and Bat Sonic Blast are not active benchmark pets.
items.impact: Pet selection completeness; not a reason to grant unselected abilities.

These are useful implementation leads with rank/cost/cooldown data, not an unanswered question about whether any new abilities exist. The public issue records checked contain Discord pointers rather than independently readable test results.
review.remaining: Verify each family/teaching chain against current client rows and actual tame availability; do not enable unavailable exotic pets from a retained record.
review.implementation: Implement supported families individually. Start with damage/resource effects whose teaching and child records agree; keep control-only effects outside the current DPS queue. The commented-out old Howl implementation is not a suitable current implementation.

tests.requires: Current family, teaching, child-spell, cost and cooldown records.
tests.measure: Produce one supported-rank matrix per family and implement only joined learning paths. Separate direct values from scripted behavior.

tests.requires: A family actually tameable by level 20 and its first trained rank.
tests.measure: Confirm learning, resource cost and damage/cooldown for that family. This does not establish higher-rank availability.

items.title: Dodge-triggered Mongoose Bite window
items.question: Can a dodge activate Defensive State when its aura is initially inactive?
items.current_model: The dodge callback is attached to the conditional aura itself; Expose Prey separately opens the window. The current stationary DPS encounter does not exercise incoming dodges.
items.impact: Solo/reactive Hunter support, not a demonstrated current ranking gain.

review.answer: Code inspection settles the reachability question: core registers OnSpellHitTaken callbacks on aura activation and removes them on deactivation. The inactive Defensive State aura therefore cannot observe the dodge that should initially activate it. Expose Prey is a separate working activation path.
review.remaining: A focused regression and permanent listener implementation, not a server-behavior investigation.
review.implementation: Move the dodge listener to an always-active trigger while retaining the conditional five-second window. The current un-attacked Hunter benchmark does not exercise this defect.

tests.requires: Hunter with an initially inactive Defensive State aura.
tests.measure: Dispatch an incoming dodge, verify Mongoose eligibility for five seconds, expiry, reset and independence from Expose Prey.

review.code_ready: Move Mongoose Bite's incoming-dodge listener onto an always-active trigger so the first dodge can open its window.

items.title: Demoralizing Screech target AP debuff
items.question: Does the pet apply its sourced AP reduction as well as damage?
items.current_model: Damage/rank values are modeled; the target AP reduction is not complete.
items.impact: Tank/solo mitigation with a Screech pet, not selected Cat damage.

review.answer: The AP reduction is explicit client data, not an unknown formula. Teaching spell 24582 points to active rank-four spell 24579: a 30-second AP aura, base -198 at level 56 with -1.6 per level through 60. The implementation deals damage only. Rank-one active spell 24423 also has a sourced ten-second cooldown; the cooldown is not an accidental Classic inheritance.
review.remaining: Implement rank growth, area scope and AP-debuff exclusivity. Correct the level-25 ID lookup, whose current map uses key 15.
review.implementation: Use the active child rather than its teaching spell as the behavior source. This is optional Screech-pet mitigation, not a change to the selected Cat's damage or a free raid debuff.

tests.requires: Screech pet and controlled target AP with another AP-reduction provider.
tests.measure: Check rank-level growth, 30-second expiry, area coverage and strongest-effect handling; verify that disabling the selected pet removes only its effect.

review.code_ready: Implement the active Screech rank's sourced AP debuff and fix the level-25 lookup key; do not grant it without the appropriate pet.

items.title: Fingers of Frost in-flight timing
items.question: Does a cast begun before a chill proc benefit from or consume the resulting charge?
items.current_model: Retains the current event-order interpretation with two charges at max rank. Client charge count does not establish cast-start versus impact timing.
items.impact: Frost/Arcane–Frost proc usage and apparent hybrid gains.

review.answer: The current proc records establish charge counts and duration, but not the treatment of a cast already underway when the preceding projectile lands. The code deliberately excludes that cast from Shatter and charge consumption. Neither client flags nor an unrelated expansion's 'ghost charge' behavior establishes that decision for Forever.
review.remaining: Cast-start versus impact/consumption ordering.
review.implementation: Keep the interpretation disclosed; do not promote it to a verified property of Arcane–Frost.

tests.requires: Level 30, one point in Fingers, Frostbolt and precise cast/impact/aura timestamps.
tests.measure: Compare waiting for impact with immediately starting the next cast, at short and long range. Count charge removal and Shatter outcomes for the already-started cast.

tests.requires: Level 31 for the second charge, unless later beta access is announced.
tests.measure: Repeat with two charges; do not assume the one-charge observation establishes simultaneous refresh behavior.

items.title: Frostfire cross-school scripts
items.question: Which Fire/Frost talents and Tier effects stack on Frostfire beyond explicitly named client masks?
items.current_model: Explicitly supported interactions are modeled; unresolved cross-school server behavior is not proof that conditional Frostfire research is deployable.
items.impact: Alternate Frostfire hybrids, not the full-rank Arcane–Frost identity by itself.

review.answer: This should not remain a blanket 'does Frostfire work with talents?' question. The client and existing implementation explicitly include Improved Fireball, Fire/Frost school matching, Hot Streak and the named Missile Barrage/Fingers Tier additions. Improved Frostbolt is not granted as a second cast-time reduction. The unresolved portion is scripted interaction and proc ordering beyond these explicit inclusions.
review.remaining: Any claimed interaction without a matching current family mask or named Tier effect, and interactions with unresolved Fingers timing.
review.implementation: Keep a per-effect inclusion table rather than retesting all known school/mask matches. Audit exact masks offline before requesting an experiment; do not use old low-rank research as proof of all interactions.

tests.requires: Current spell-family masks and the individual role Tier descriptions.
tests.measure: Enumerate each proposed Frostfire modifier and its positive/negative mask match; isolate genuine script-only gaps.

tests.requires: Frostfire first learned at level 40 and each disputed talent/Tier effect.
tests.measure: Test only the remaining script interactions independently at full rank with fixed school power.

items.title: Hot Streak interruption and new-charge ordering
items.question: What happens if accelerated Pyroblast is interrupted or new stacks arrive during its cast?
items.current_model: A completed Pyroblast consumes all Hot Streak stacks. Persistent free acceleration is fixed; interruption/in-flight edge behavior is not measured.
items.impact: Fire edge cases; not a reopening of the confirmed consumption fix.

review.answer: Completed-Pyro consumption is already supported and fixed. The current client child 400625 has one proc charge, three stack capacity and a 20-second duration; the engine's 20 seconds agrees, while the UI's 15-second talent description is stale. Interrupt retention is irrelevant to an uninterrupted reference fight, but an earlier projectile creating a new stack during Pyro can occur there.
review.remaining: Whether a newly earned in-flight stack is also consumed; interrupted casts matter only for interruption scenarios.
review.implementation: Correct the stale display text separately. Do not undo completed-Pyro consumption or call the narrow ordering question a persistent-Hot-Streak uncertainty.

tests.requires: Level 25+ Hot Streak/Pyro build and cast/impact/aura logs.
tests.measure: Start accelerated Pyro while an earlier Fire projectile is in flight; compare aura stacks at impact and completion. Separately cancel Pyro if interruption support is being evaluated.

review.code_ready: Update Hot Streak's stale 15-second talent description to the sourced 20 seconds already used by the engine.

items.title: Clearcasting and Missile Barrage event ordering
items.question: How do channel ticks, last-charge consumption and simultaneous procs interact?
items.current_model: Clearcasting consumes on the next eligible paid damage cast with a one-second trigger ICD. Explicit Missile Barrage timing is retained.
items.impact: Arcane and hybrid resources; ordinary persistent-Clearcasting bug is already fixed.

review.answer: The question combines two access levels. Arcane Concentration and ordinary Arcane Missiles are testable now; Missile Barrage is a level-25 talent and does not require max-level access. Current code excludes Arcane Missiles from the ordinary Clearcasting proc callback and consumes eligible Clearcasting at cast-complete. Client percentages alone do not resolve the channel's proc opportunity or ordering.
review.remaining: Whether/how Missiles proc Clearcasting, and consumption when Barrage makes a channel free or another proc arrives during it.
review.implementation: Separate channel proc opportunity from the already repaired persistent-Clearcasting bug. Do not infer a Classic 1.5%-per-tick rule from the commented-out code.

tests.requires: Arcane Concentration, Arcane Missiles and mana/aura/tick logging without other proc talents.
tests.measure: Cast isolated complete and cancelled channels; count Clearcasting procs and identify whether a pre-existing proc is spent at channel start or completion.

tests.requires: Level 25+ Missile Barrage, controlled proc state.
tests.measure: Compare channels with Clearcasting only, Barrage only and both, including a new proc during the channel. Record actual mana debit rather than tooltip cost.

items.title: Combustion multi-target charge handling
items.question: Do multiple hits from one Flamestrike independently add and consume Combustion charges?
items.current_model: The callback handles each landed Fire hit individually and carries an explicit Flamestrike TODO.
items.impact: Fire AoE, not the one-target reference rotation.

review.answer: The open question is per-target charge handling for one area cast. The current Fire reference is single-target and does not use Flamestrike. The implementation TODO does not establish a defect in that reference DPS result.
review.remaining: Multi-target Fire behavior, if a Fire AoE workload is added.
review.implementation: Remove this from the current benchmark-blocking queue while retaining it as an explicit AoE coverage limit.

tests.requires: Level 40 Combustion and a future multi-target Fire scenario.
tests.measure: Compare aura charge changes for one Flamestrike hitting one versus several enemies; distinguish noncritical hits, critical hits and periodic ticks.

items.title: Shadow Word: Death script value 150
items.question: What does the additional dummy/script value do?
items.current_model: Four learned ranks, sourced damage/cost/cooldown, backlash and Early Demise are implemented. No extra execute multiplier is inferred from 150.
items.impact: Shadow damage/execute behavior and possible missing scripted behavior.

review.answer: The raw record identifies 150 specifically as effect type 77 (script effect), separate from direct damage and the 10% backlash dummy. It is not a 150% damage modifier in the client effect system. Neither the current tooltip nor the reviewed public evidence supplies its server script.
review.remaining: What script 77 does, if anything material beyond the described Death behavior.
review.implementation: Continue omitting an invented execute multiplier. This is a concrete script gap, not missing rank/cost/coefficient data.

tests.requires: Death rank one at level 32; fixed SP, talents and target mitigation.
tests.measure: Compare damage and backlash above/below execute thresholds, lethal/nonlethal hits and cooldown behavior. Subtract ordinary Early Demise and damage-range effects before attributing anything to 150.

items.title: Death backlash and Dark Sacrifice modifiers
items.question: Which damage, resistance, absorb and survival rules affect these self-costs?
items.current_model: Death uses its implemented health-backlash interpretation; Dark Sacrifice uses unmodified client amounts and cannot crit. Non-tanking DPS does not model a constrained healer budget.
items.impact: Priest resources/survival, not enemy damage from self-hits.

The current unlimited-healing DPS scenario does not rank Priests by surviving their self-costs, so exact backlash mitigation is not a direct DPS multiplier. Dark Sacrifice's actual health-to-mana return still matters to resources and is a distinct, earlier-access test.
review.remaining: Self-cost mitigation/absorb/lethality for survival support, and any Dark Sacrifice resource dependence on effective damage.
review.implementation: Keep the sourced noncrit/unmodified interpretation as a disclosed model; do not fold self-damage into DPS or dismiss mana-return behavior as immaterial.

tests.requires: Level-20 Undead Priest with Dark Sacrifice, fixed maximum health and Spirit, uncapped mana, with/without a controlled absorb.
tests.measure: Record each health and mana delta, then repeat near mana cap and low health. Separate periodic dummy returns from ordinary Spirit regeneration.

tests.requires: Death at level 32+, and controlled resistance/absorb/damage-reduction states.
tests.measure: Measure nonlethal, killing-blow and avoided-hit backlash; include lethal self-cost only when evaluating finite-healing survival.

items.title: Divine Spirit's baseline acquisition
items.question: Can Priests train Divine Spirit after its talent was removed?
items.current_model: External 40 Spirit coverage is assumed; surviving class-skill rows are not conclusive trainer evidence. Removed Fortitude improvement talents do not multiply the current sourced buff again.
items.impact: Caster/Warlock resources and Spirit-based effects.

review.answer: Blizzard's official Deep Dive recap explicitly says Divine Spirit, Blessing of Kings and Improved Mark of the Wild are baseline. This resolves intended Divine Spirit availability without requiring a future trainer screenshot. Current client ranks separately give 17/23/33/40 Spirit at levels 30/40/50/60.

items.title: Mutilate off-hand flat damage and Cold Blood
items.question: Does the off-hand penalty include Mutilate's flat bonus, and does Cold Blood cover both strikes?
items.current_model: Retains the current main-hand consumption and off-hand flat-component treatment. Puncturing Wounds already applies to both hands.
items.impact: Mutilate damage and cooldown value.

review.answer: Cold Blood's current family modifier covers the Mutilate family and has one proc charge; Mutilate dispatches two child attacks. That establishes eligibility but not whether the server holds the guaranteed crit for both children before consuming it. The off-hand's weapon-plus-flat ordering likewise cannot be established from a parent dummy description alone.
review.remaining: Paired-child charge consumption and off-hand flat-component penalty.
review.implementation: Keep the current MH-only Cold Blood interpretation disclosed. Do not use an inherited expansion's paired-strike behavior as a Forever answer.

tests.requires: Level 30 Mutilate/Cold Blood allocation, two known daggers, fixed AP and target armor.
tests.measure: Record both child hit/crit outcomes with and without Cold Blood. Swap hand placements and vary AP independently to distinguish flat bonus from weapon contribution.

tests.requires: Higher Mutilate ranks.
tests.measure: Verify that the higher flat component follows the low-rank ordering; do not repeat already settled proc timing unless a patch changes it.

items.title: Poison charge depletion
items.question: Can poison charges expire during a supported long encounter?
items.current_model: Finite item charges are not consumed. Current client charge counts are retained as data, not runtime limits.
items.impact: Long fights and very fast attack/proc setups.

review.answer: Charge counts are available: current top-rank Instant and Deadly give 175 and 180. Existing 300-second results average at most 92.29 Instant attempts and 96.05 Deadly applications across the three Rogue builds/races. That is substantial headroom, not a proof that no individual long or unusually fast fight can deplete a coating.
review.remaining: Per-iteration tails, per-hand attribution and reapplication behavior for long fights.
review.implementation: Lower the immediate benchmark priority. Charge depletion is an offline accounting task with known limits; it does not require launch access to begin. Count poison applications, not Deadly tick events.

tests.requires: Per-hand application counters and current coating limits.
tests.measure: Record per-iteration maxima for baseline and fastest sensitivity scenarios; add finite charges/reapplication before claiming coverage of arbitrarily long encounters.

tests.requires: A low-rank finite coating and combat/charge logging.
tests.measure: Only if consumption semantics remain unclear: distinguish eligible weapon swings, proc attempts and landed poison hits, including resisted applications.

items.title: Deadly Poison V acquisition
items.question: Is the highest poison available without an unavailable raid book?
items.current_model: Retained spell/item records do not independently establish acquisition in the allowed content.
items.impact: Conditional highest-rank poison availability; normalized item gear does not make unavailable spells trainable.

review.answer: Current spell/item records establish Deadly Poison V's existence and values, not its obtainable recipe. The public item page still carries older damage/charge text and is not a current trainer or loot-source confirmation. Normalized equipment does not settle spell acquisition.
review.remaining: A current trainer, vendor, recipe or loot source for rank five in the allowed content.
review.implementation: Retain the availability caveat rather than treating the item database as a learning path. Resolve through source data first; if unavailable at launch, use the highest actually learnable rank.

tests.requires: Current trainer/vendor/recipe or loot-source export.
tests.measure: Join the learned recipe to an obtainable source; distinguish the crafted poison item from its recipe.

tests.requires: Level-60 Rogue and relevant trainer/vendor/content access if no source export resolves it first.
tests.measure: Confirm acquisition without an unavailable raid book and record the obtainable rank.

items.title: Hack and Slash hand scope and ICD
items.question: Is the 200-ms extra-attack ICD real, and how do mixed weapon bonuses apply?
items.current_model: Retains the inherited ICD and current hand-type gates. Talent rank amounts are sourced, event/stacking semantics are not fully measured.
items.impact: Combat and mixed-weapon alternatives.

review.answer: The 200-ms ICD is explicitly present in SpellAuraOptions for both parent 13960 and triggered aura 1290312. It is no longer merely an inherited assumption. Dagger/fist and mace child auras also have equipped-weapon masks; those masks do not alone settle every mixed-hand, character-wide application.
review.remaining: Mixed-hand crit and armor-ignore scope, not the sourced ICD.
review.implementation: Retain the 200-ms gate. Narrow the experiment to mixed weapons and any observed contradiction; do not spend a large sample re-estimating a value already supplied by the current client.

tests.requires: One point in Hack and Slash at level 30; matched dagger/fist, mace and sword pairs.
tests.measure: Swap MH/OH placement. Compare each hand's crit and armor-sensitive damage, plus a non-weapon spell control; separate a displayed character-sheet bonus from hand-specific outcomes.

tests.requires: Level 34 for all five ranks, if no expanded beta access.
tests.measure: Verify full-rank magnitude only if the one-point hand-scope test leaves nonlinear behavior unresolved.

items.title: Premeditation expiry and Feint threat
items.question: Are temporary combo points expired and Feint's threat reduction applied?
items.current_model: Premeditation grants points without the sourced 20-second expiry; Feint does not apply its actual threat drop.
items.impact: Prepull/long-idle Rogue setups and threat-constrained encounters, not ordinary sustained damage alone.

review.answer: These are known missing implementations, not unknown game rules. Current Rogue damage requests do not use Feint or intentionally hold prepull Premeditation points past their expiry; their damage ranking is not threat-limited. Neither omission presently explains the benchmark order.
review.remaining: Temporary-point expiry and Feint's negative threat for future long-idle or threat-constrained setups.
review.implementation: Retain both in the implementation backlog, outside the current in-game test queue. A Feint implementation also needs to avoid granting damage-proc eligibility merely because its placeholder uses a melee proc mask.

tests.requires: Temporary CP ownership/expiry and explicit threat accounting.
tests.measure: Verify spending before expiry, expiration without erasing unrelated points, target/reset behavior and an actual threat decrease from Feint without damage/proc inflation.

items.title: Blade Flurry copied-damage modifiers
items.question: Should copied damage receive attacker or target modifiers a second time?
items.current_model: The inherited secondary-damage path explicitly flags possible double dipping; it is not settled by matching one-target tests.
items.impact: Combat two-target damage and target-armor differences.

review.answer: The code path does reapply ordinary modifiers: it removes only the first target's resistance multiplier from copied damage, then passes that value through another normal damage calculation. The current client parent is a proc aura and does not supply a copied-damage formula. This identifies the risk precisely but does not establish the intended server exception. One-target reference results never exercise the copy.
review.remaining: Which attacker and target multipliers belong on the copied hit.
review.implementation: Do not claim a verified correction from the TODO alone. Keep the question in two-target Rogue coverage, not as a blocker for single-target results.

tests.requires: Level-30 Blade Flurry, two controlled targets and a removable damage modifier.
tests.measure: Compare primary and copied hits against equal and different armor. Toggle one attacker modifier and one target modifier separately; compare ratios rather than unrelated DPS totals.

items.title: Windfury Weapon extra-attack handling
items.question: Are its proc attacks ordinary extra swings or yellow attacks, with which trigger/cooldown rules?
items.current_model: Retains the existing proc implementation; no dual-wield Shaman or off-hand attack is granted. Totem is a separate buff and cannot proc on the owner's Windfury-imbued weapon.
items.impact: Enhancement weapon/proc value; not the same question as Totem charges.

review.answer: Following the actual enchant chain resolves the cooldown: Windfury enchants 283/284/525/1669 point to aura 439431, whose current ProcCategoryRecovery is 1500 ms and ProcChance is 20. Its effect is a server dummy. Looking only at legacy extra-attack spell 8233 would miss that active path. The one-and-a-half-second ICD is supported; the yellow-versus-white resolution remains unmeasured.
review.remaining: The dummy's generated attack outcome table, swing timing, recursion and rank/AP routing.
review.implementation: Retain the sourced chance and ICD. Keep special-attack resolution qualified; neither blindly restore Classic white attacks nor cite a SoD resemblance as proof.

tests.requires: Level-30 Windfury Weapon, a known two-handed or one-handed MH weapon, no other extra-attack effect.
tests.measure: Record the proc's two damage events, misses/crits/glances, regular swing timing and proc spacing. Change AP independently and keep the initial rank distinct from its max-scaled tooltip.

tests.requires: Later imbue ranks and the actual Windfury Totem provider.
tests.measure: Confirm rank/AP routing and that an own Windfury weapon excludes the separate Totem benefit.

items.title: Owned buff-totem effects and replacement
items.question: Does an APL-cast buff totem actually supply its rank-correct party buff and remove its previous owned buff?
items.current_model: Some owned totems are tracking auras while raid/party settings supply external buffs. Owned Mana Tide/Healing Stream cancellation is implemented; owned Mana Spring regeneration itself remains incomplete.
items.impact: Self-sufficient Shaman/tank-party scenarios and low-rank totem choices; externally supplied ranking buffs must not double count.

review.answer: This is a provider-model gap with available rank data.
