Owned Windfury currently creates a tracking aura rather than the rank-correct functional buff; owned Mana Spring likewise does not supply its recorded regeneration. External raid settings are a separate source and must not be silently replaced or duplicated.
review.remaining: An implementation that tracks owned versus external providers and their expiry/replacement independently.
review.implementation: Use shared functional buff implementations with provider ownership, current ranks and exclusive categories. Preserve externally supplied reference support; do not grant both Windfury and Grace merely because one source is an APL totem.

tests.requires: Owned low/high-rank totems plus independent external providers.
tests.measure: Check actual stats/resource returns, replacement, expiry and recall. Removing an owned provider must not delete a surviving external provider or leave its own effect permanent.

items.title: Fire Nova threat owner
items.question: Is Fire Nova threat attributed to the Shaman or the active Fire totem?
items.current_model: Requires a live owned Fire totem; damage and threat are credited to the Shaman.
items.impact: Threat-constrained encounters, not damage amount in a stationary unthreatened DPS run.

review.answer: The unresolved issue is threat ownership, not Nova damage or its owned-Fire-totem requirement. No current Shaman tank row is ranked, and stationary Shaman DPS has no aggro constraint. Changing ownership would not alter that damage comparison.
review.remaining: Threat attribution for a future Shaman tank or aggro-constrained workload.
review.implementation: Keep the limitation visible but remove it from the current DPS-blocking queue. Do not change the verified live-totem requirement.

tests.requires: Fire Nova and a live Fire totem, an isolated enemy and a threat API observer.
tests.measure: When threat-constrained support is needed, measure owner and totem threat before/after Nova with no other damage; repeat after totem replacement.

items.title: Demonic Brand power source and threat
items.question: Whose school power does Brand read, can it crit, and what threat multiplier applies?
items.current_model: Sourced level-60 base/coefficient and target-scoped charges; reads owner matching-school power at hit time, with provisional pet school assignment, noncrit handling and 3× threat.
items.impact: Demonic Pact pet damage and threat; its formula is not just flat demo damage anymore.

review.answer: Description variables explicitly provide the level term and 0.078 school-power term; child records are always-hit Fire and Shadow spells. Those records do not specify whose runtime power the script reads, an exact 3x threat multiplier or a blanket cannot-crit flag. The model's unconditional noncrit and 3x threat remain interpretations, not extracted constants.
review.remaining: Owner-versus-demon power source, crit eligibility and actual threat/attribution.
review.implementation: Keep the sourced formula separate from its runtime context. Do not require max-level access for the first useful test: Brand is available from level 25.

tests.requires: Level 25+ Brand, Imp and a melee demon, controlled owner school power and pet modifiers.
tests.measure: Separate normal pet attacks from Brand events. Vary owner power, record Brand crits and threat, and test a second target without a Brand.

tests.requires: Max-level pet ranks and relevant Tier effects.
tests.measure: Verify the level extrapolation and Tier interactions rather than rediscovering the basic power owner.

items.title: Incinerate's Immolate bonus scope
items.question: Does the 25% Immolate bonus multiply base damage only or the whole SP-scaled hit?
items.current_model: Retains the current implementation pending a controlled coefficient test; tooltip wording alone was insufficient.
items.impact: Destruction and alternate Fire rotations.

review.answer: The current client encodes the Immolate bonus as a 25-valued dummy, not a standard final-damage multiplier. The engine multiplies only the random base before adding SP. The public tooltip repeats the bonus but does not resolve that ordering; no controlled Forever result was found in the reviewed public sources.
review.remaining: Base-only versus full-hit multiplier.
review.implementation: Do not import another expansion's formula. A two-SP-level comparison can settle this directly.

tests.requires: Level-40 Incinerate and two known SP totals on the same target.
tests.measure: Measure with/without Immolate at each SP total. Compare the slopes, not just one tooltip-range average; retain identical damage talents and mitigation.

items.title: Wrack's amplified DoT scope
items.question: Which other Shadow DoTs receive its amplification, and exactly when does cancellation remove it?
items.current_model: Channel cancellation works; its modifier ends on cancellation. Current scope is not independently verified for every effect, especially Doom.
items.impact: Affliction channel/DoT interactions.

review.answer: The current Wrack modifier is aura 271 with family mask 0x402. Joining the spell-family records selects Corruption (0x2) and Agony (0x400), not Doom or Drain Life/Soul. Wowhead's affected-spell list independently matches that narrower scope. The engine instead accepts almost any other owned Shadow spell with a DoT. Channel cancellation is already implemented.
review.remaining: Correct the overly broad mask and test cancellation; no server experiment is needed to implement the current explicit client scope.
review.implementation: Restrict the modifier to the sourced family, retaining owner/target checks. Reconcile the level-40 learning record with the engine's level-60 registration metadata. Treat any later server evidence of broader behavior as a versioned contradiction, not the default assumption.

tests.requires: Controlled owned Corruption, Agony, Doom and another caster's DoT.
tests.measure: Verify positive/negative modifier scope, immediate removal on channel cancellation and low-level availability at its actual learning level.

review.code_ready: Limit Wrack's amplification to Corruption and Agony and reconcile its level-40 acquisition metadata.

items.title: Spellstone's Fire/Shadow mask
items.question: Does Spellstone increase both Fire and Shadow power despite Shadow-only wording?
items.current_model: Uses the client's Fire+Shadow mask plus casting speed. Current saved profiles do not select it.
items.impact: Optional weapon imbue, not a current baseline modifier.

review.answer: The captured effect uses school mask 36, explicitly Fire plus Shadow, and the implementation follows it. This is a defensible data-led answer despite narrower prose; no current saved profile selects Spellstone. A stale pre-Forever off-hand Spellstone page is not evidence against the new weapon enchant.
review.remaining: Only a contrary server observation or later corrected effect would require reopening the selected mask.
review.implementation: Retain the client mask and document the tooltip conflict. Remove this from the required benchmark experiment queue rather than waiting for launch to approve a sourced optional effect.

items.title: Fel Armor acquisition
items.question: Is Fel Armor actually available rather than a retained rune record?
items.current_model: Not granted; the misleading duplicate Demon Armor selector was removed.
items.impact: Optional Warlock defensive/resource setup.

review.answer: Fel Armor 403619 survives as a rune-era spell/skill record, but no verified ordinary learning path was found. Current public spellbook coverage instead lists Demon Armor. The absence of a known source is not proof that Fel Armor can never be added, but it is sufficient reason not to grant it in this benchmark.
review.remaining: A new verified Forever acquisition path, if one appears.
review.implementation: Keep it excluded and the duplicate selector removed. Move this to a source-watch list, not a mandatory launch experiment for every Warlock.

tests.requires: A current trainer/quest/skill-path source identifying this spell, not just a same-name retained row.
tests.measure: Reopen only when that acquisition chain exists; then verify effects and exclusivity before adding a selectable option.

items.title: Improved Imp's extra dummy effect
items.question: Does the undocumented -300/-700/-1000 effect shorten Firebolt casts?
items.current_model: The suspected cast-time modifier is not inferred from the dummy values alone.
items.impact: Live Imp alternatives; sacrificed Imps do not gain combat damage.

review.answer: The active trait does contain the -300/-700/-1000 dummy, but neither current prose nor effect type identifies its script. It cannot be safely converted into cast-time milliseconds. Separately, the documented Firebolt bonus is a normal damage modifier, while the code scales only base damage; that distinct implementation issue is recorded as WL-008.
review.remaining: The dummy's actual effect and the live Imp's cast/recast behavior.
review.implementation: Do not invent a cast-speed change from the negative numbers. Keep the documented damage-scope correction separate from this unresolved script.

tests.requires: A live Imp, ranks 0/1/2/3 of Improved Imp, fixed owner/pet haste and mana.
tests.measure: Record Firebolt cast start/end and the interval before the next cast. Distinguish a shorter cast from removal of the engine's artificial 200-ms recast delay.

items.title: Soul Shards and kill-triggered resource effects
items.question: Can the simulator represent shard costs/refunds and qualifying kills?
items.current_model: No finite Soul Shard inventory or full kill-event model; some shard-related talents have no meaningful cost effect.
items.impact: Short-fight openers, repeated summons and execute/kill scenarios.

review.answer: Finite shards and qualifying kills are absent engine resources/events, not an unknown damage coefficient. Current reference comparisons effectively assume adequate starting shards and do not model add kills or repeated resummon depletion. That assumption can be made explicit without a live raid test.
review.remaining: Inventory bounds and kill/refund events for shard-constrained or resummoning scenarios.
review.implementation: First count shard-spending casts in saved profiles against a declared starting inventory. Add costs/refunds before claiming long-fight or repeated-summon support; do not derive free shards from a target that never dies.

tests.requires: Declared starting shards and sourced per-spell reagent/refund rules.
tests.measure: Check inventory conservation, cast eligibility at zero, reset and exact qualifying kill events; keep assumed unlimited-shard reference results clearly labeled.

items.title: Boss attack tables
items.question: What are level-60 miss, dodge, parry, crit-suppression and glancing rules against level-63 targets?
items.current_model: Forever uses the explicit attack-table changes in the engine, with remaining inherited formulas. Demo columns and research checklists do not establish every boss case.
items.impact: All melee, ranged and tank comparisons; hit caps and crit value.

review.answer: The updated attack-table issue now includes initial +3-level results consistent with the Classic table. Its proposed percentages and sample-size plan are not a completed level-63 test. The report explicitly excludes currently broken glancing damage.
review.remaining: Boss-level tables, suppression and glancing damage after the beta fix.
review.implementation: Do not tune to the acknowledged glancing-damage bug or treat the issue's hypothetical table as measured coefficients.

tests.requires: Known skill/hit, an equal-level and a +3-level target, recorded facing.
tests.measure: Count white/special/ranged outcomes separately; compare queued and unqueued attacks. This supplies a low-level table, not a level-63 certification.

tests.requires: Level-60 characters and level-63 targets on a build without the known glancing defect.
tests.measure: Repeat outcome and crit-suppression counts; compare damage of glances with ordinary hits at fixed AP.

items.title: Energy regeneration and haste
items.question: Does general haste increase Energy regeneration, and do attack-speed-only effects leave it unchanged?
items.current_model: 10 Energy/sec integrated in 100-ms steps; general haste provisionally increases the rate. Slice and Dice, Berserking and attack-only enchants do not. The step size is not a measured server tick.
items.impact: Feral and all Rogue builds; haste and resource value.

review.answer: PowerType establishes the base 10 Energy/sec, not the haste coefficient. The previously analyzed 1% sample spans both 10 and 10.1/sec within endpoint quantization error. No new controlled source in the reviewed issue collections settles the distinction.
review.remaining: General-haste scaling, distinct from attack-speed effects.
review.implementation: Keep the existing haste multiplier explicitly provisional; do not import retail resource rules as a fact.

tests.requires: Two known general-haste totals, identical resource talents, uncapped recovery windows and precise resource timestamps.
tests.measure: Repeat matched recovery cycles from low Energy to below the cap, with no attacks or refunds. Aggregate endpoint uncertainty; a single rounded 1% window is insufficient. Run an attack-speed-only control separately.

items.title: Optional MP5-per-second interpretation
items.question: Does a flat displayed MP5 point restore one mana per five seconds or per second?
items.current_model: Ordinary MP5/5 per second is the default. The explicit optional mode multiplies only the MP5 stat contribution by five; it is off in rankings.
items.impact: Mana users if enabled; does not establish a current ranking error.

review.answer: The beta report supplies 0/2/4 gear-MP5 controls, a combat-log attachment and video; a project contributor acknowledges an engineering bug. It explicitly reports normal five-second behavior for Blessing of Wisdom and Mageblood. This is evidence for a gear-specific beta defect, not a universal redefinition of MP5.
review.remaining: Whether the gear bug has been deployed as fixed on a later build. That is a beta-version watch, not a prerequisite for the intended ordinary-MP5 benchmark.
review.implementation: The default MP5/5 rule remains appropriate for the intended model. The optional uniform fivefold setting is a hypothetical sensitivity mode, not a faithful emulation of the reported gear-only bug; its description should say so.

tests.requires: Only if reproducing a particular live beta build is needed; gear with a known MP5 delta and a separate Wisdom/Mageblood control.
tests.measure: Compare uncapped regeneration while continuously spending mana. Keep Spirit fixed and record the exact client build; distinguish item MP5 from buff MP5.

items.title: Dynamic periodic damage boundaries
items.question: Which damage components update during an existing DoT, and which cast-specific bonuses remain attached?
items.current_model: Forever periodic damage uses dynamic stats/modifiers under the adopted no-snapshot model, with explicit cast-specific effects and Ignite exclusions. Deep Wounds also reads current weapon/AP state.
items.impact: All DoT builds; temporary buffs, weapon swaps and poison upkeep.
legacy: T52 in in_game_checks.md (dynamic DoTs) / T02 Deep Wounds follow-up / T35 periodic scope

review.answer: The Forever Hunter wiki explicitly describes dynamic Sting RAP and periodic crit. Public reports also distinguish intended dynamic Thorns/Ret Aura scaling from their beta snapshot bug. These support the ordinary no-snapshot rule, but not every charged-cast or proc-payload exception.
review.remaining: Narrow cast-specific exceptions belong to Eureka, Inner Focus and the individual proc records, not a blanket retest of every ordinary DoT.
review.implementation: Keep ordinary dynamic periodic damage as the reference rule. Do not multiply an already calculated Ignite/Deep Wounds payload again merely because ordinary DoTs are dynamic.

items.title: Tea and conjured-item shared cooldowns
items.question: Which consumables share cooldowns with Thistle Tea, including prepull uses?
items.current_model: Rogues and Cats can use the sourced 100 Energy, five-minute Tea. The inherited cross-conjured shared-category handling is retained.
items.impact: Feral/Rogue resource plans and mixed consumable configurations.

review.answer: All 31 current Tea profiles select Tea as their sole conjured item; the registration switch allows one selected conjured consumable. Their five-minute scenario has no Tea prepull, and Tea's own five-minute cooldown prevents another use within the fight. The speculative cross-conjured cooldown does not constrain these requests.
review.remaining: Shared-category behavior matters only for a future mixed-conjured or different prepull setup.
review.implementation: Keep the sourced Tea amount and personal cooldown. Move the cross-item interaction out of the current benchmark test queue; do not call its actual server category measured.

items.title: Mana restoration threat
items.question: Which mana returns generate threat, who receives it, and is it divided between enemies?
items.current_model: The inherited accounting assigns 0.5 threat per effective mana gained to each enemy for non-exempt returns. Passive regeneration and attributed Innervate are excluded; Vampiric Touch has separate ownership. These source exemptions and per-enemy allocation are not established Forever behavior.
items.impact: Tank TPS and rotation comparisons: wasting mana can increase subsequent effective restoration and its credited threat without improving damage or survival.

review.answer: There is a public resource/healing-threat report with API observations and a video. Both its observed grouped allocation and its expected even allocation distribute a finite total; neither adds the full total independently to every enemy. The current AddMana/ApplyAOEThreat path does the latter. Source exemptions and ownership are separate questions.
review.remaining: Source-specific threat amounts/exemptions and whether live mixed-creature grouping has been fixed. The supplied report is community evidence, not an official statement of the complete threat system.
review.implementation: Treat multi-target resource-threat duplication as a source-supported correction candidate, with a focused total-conservation test before changing tank results. Do not copy the reported creature-grouping bug into the benchmark.

tests.requires: A mana user, effective mana potions, threat API readings and one versus several engaged enemies.
tests.measure: Measure total and per-enemy threat from one isolated return, including same-type and mixed-type packs. A mana-capped use is the wasted-resource control.

items.title: Level-60 outgoing rage normalization
items.question: Do the measured low-level speed-based rage rates persist at level 60?
items.current_model: Damage-independent rage: base weapon speed × 4.5 for two-handers, or × (4.5/1.3) for one-hand main hand. Crits/glances do not increase it; haste changes swing frequency, not rage per hit.
items.impact: All Warrior damage, gear selection and rotation decisions.

review.answer: Newer public logs extend the evidence beyond the original captures, and the no-extra-rage-on-crit report was explicitly answered as intended behavior. Speed-based damage-independent rage is well supported at tested beta levels; max-level extrapolation remains a distinct assumption.
review.remaining: The level-60 rate, not the already answered low-level damage-versus-rage question.
review.implementation: No change to the current base-speed rule. Do not spend another current-beta experiment rediscovering the same damage independence.

tests.requires: A known weapon retained across levels and no other rage gains.
tests.measure: Optional extrapolation checkpoint: compare uncapped rage per landed swing before and after leveling. This does not certify level 60.

tests.requires: Level 60 and known one- and two-handed base speeds.
tests.measure: Measure uncapped ordinary swings while varying damage independently; test the existing 4.5 and 4.5/1.3 rates rather than fitting a damage formula anew.

items.title: Off-hand and extra-swing rage
items.question: What rage do off-hand, avoided and proc-generated swings award?
items.current_model: Half-rate off-hand before the sourced Dual Wield Specialization multiplier; avoided autos award none. This is not a measured complete level-60 Fury rule.
items.impact: Fury, Windfury and weapon-proc value.

review.answer: The half-rate off-hand rule now has Forever log support, not just a Cataclysm analogy. An independently inspected public dual-wield sample has dominant clusters of 3.2878 rage with reported 1.9 speed and 6.91 with 2.0 speed: approximately 1.7304 and 3.455 rage per weapon-second. The public analysis reports additional matching weapon pairs.
review.remaining: Proc-generated extra swings, the Dual Wield Specialization interaction, and max-level extrapolation are not established by ordinary low-level off-hand samples.
review.implementation: Retain the half-rate model, upgrading its evidence status only for ordinary tested off-hand swings. Do not describe all extra-attack rage as verified.

tests.requires: A sourced extra-attack effect actually available by level 30, and separate MH/OH events.
tests.measure: Isolate extra swings from regular autos and energizes. If no suitable effect is obtainable, defer that subtest rather than substituting ordinary swings.

tests.requires: Relevant talent ranks and the actual raid Windfury buff.
tests.measure: Repeat the off-hand ratio with the rage talent and test proc-generated swings, independently of damage and crit.

items.title: Flurry amount and charge events
items.question: Which events proc, refresh and spend Flurry, and does the talent curve or triggered aura determine speed?
items.current_model: 5–25% melee speed; three shared charges. White-tagged events, including avoided swings and queued replacements, consume charges without a 500-ms gate. Melee crits refill after consumption. Each Cleave target may consume a charge.
items.impact: All Flurry builds, especially dual wield and cleave.

review.answer: The linked Flurry issue and current compendium chapter explicitly remain a model/testing plan. The active Warrior tree puts the first rank behind 25 points: level 35, with rank five at 39. Ordinary haste retaining rage per swing is supported elsewhere, but does not establish every Flurry charge rule.
review.remaining: White/queued/extra-swing consumption, multi-target Cleave, refresh order and mid-swing timing.
review.implementation: Retain the current disclosed model; no source justifies changing charge logic in this research pass.

tests.requires: Warrior level 35+ for the first rank; level 39 for rank five. Later beta access could move this earlier.
tests.measure: Record aura stack changes and swing times for crits, avoided swings, paired MH/OH swings, HS and multi-target Cleave. Verify refresh/consumption ordering without assuming a 500-ms gate.

items.title: Unbridled Wrath beta fix status
items.question: Has the acknowledged lower-than-intended beta proc rate been corrected?
items.current_model: Uses intended 12% per point on ordinary landed white swings. Heroic Strike and Cleave are excluded following observed eligibility.
items.impact: Warrior rage supply; intended model may differ from a live beta bug.

review.answer: The public report distinguishes the measured beta under-proc from the intended 12%-per-point rate and documents white-hit eligibility. A contributor says the fix is for a future build, specifically not the next one. The intended simulation rule is answered; the issue's Closed label does not prove the live fix was shipped.
review.remaining: Only deployment status and separately unmeasured proc-extra-swing eligibility.
review.implementation: Keep intended 12% per point and the documented HS/Cleave exclusion. Do not reduce the model to reproduce an acknowledged transient bug.

tests.requires: Only if matching a specific live beta build is necessary; known UW rank and ordinary landed autos.
tests.measure: Count energize events, including capped zero-gain events, against eligible swings. Record the build; do not count HS/Cleave as white swings.

items.title: Furor's lower-rank Energy carryover
items.question: How are carried Energy, time out of form and the rank-dependent cap combined?
items.current_model: The helper counts all elapsed time since Cat exit, including time in Bear, and caps the regenerated component before adding carried Energy. That does not follow the captured Furor wording.
items.impact: Alternate Feral shift builds; current no-Furor profiles do not establish the rule.

review.answer: The active Furor curve and description explicitly specify the carried fraction, out-of-form rate and rank cap, excluding time in Bear as well as Cat. The present helper counts all time since Cat exit and caps only the regenerated component before adding carried Energy. This is a code/source reconciliation problem before it is a request for more gameplay footage.
review.remaining: Resolve the total-cap interpretation against the exact description and reproduce Bear-time handling. The public Cat-to-Bear report describes a live bug, not a replacement intended formula.
review.implementation: Add isolated shift-state reproductions and reconcile the helper with the captured formula before evaluating a Furor rotation. Keep current no-Furor baseline behavior separate.

tests.requires: Level-20 Druid with Cat Form and a low Furor rank.
tests.measure: Leave Cat with known Energy, compare equal waits in caster and Bear, then re-enter Cat. Include a carry-plus-wait case exceeding the rank cap.

review.code_ready: Reproduce and correct Furor's inclusion of Bear time and lower-rank carry/cap ordering against the explicit client formula.

items.title: Thick Hide Defense coefficient
items.question: What amount of armor does each Defense point contribute in each form?
items.current_model: Armor updates dynamically by form and bonus Defense, but the implementation multiplies 0.67 by rank instead of using the explicit 0.67/1.33/2.00 curve.
items.impact: Bear gearing, mitigation and normalized defensive-stat value.

review.answer: Active definition 134403 links curves 85346 and 111990. The description divides the first curve by 100, giving exactly 0.67/1.33/2 armor per bonus Defense and 1/2/3 base armor per level, multiplied by the form. This settles the scalar/unit conflict. A recent beta report independently describes the rank-three intended +2 slope and a live negative/zero-bonus bug.
review.remaining: No further experiment is needed to choose the intended coefficient. Beta deployment behavior is separate from the source formula.
review.implementation: The engine uses 0.67 times points, giving 1.34/2.01 rather than 1.33/2.00 at ranks two/three. Use the explicit rank array in a subsequent correction; do not reproduce the reported negative-defense bug.
review.code_ready: Use Thick Hide's explicit 0.67/1.33/2.00 Defense-to-armor rank array instead of 0.67 times rank.

items.title: Improved Moonfire SP scope
items.question: Does Improved Moonfire multiply only base damage or the SP contribution too?
items.current_model: Retains a base-damage modifier. Moonfury's separate school-wide modifier has already been corrected and is not the same open question.
items.impact: Balance Moonfire contribution.

review.answer: The active Improved Moonfire definition has separate critical-chance, damage and periodic-damage family modifiers, all 5/10% through its curves. The current code instead modifies only BaseDamageMultiplierAdditive. Ordinary damage-modifier semantics and the explicit periodic effect support applying the damage bonus to the SP-scaled components, rather than inventing a base-only restriction.
review.remaining: Verify the intended direct/periodic calculation path in a targeted native test before changing results; no zero-coefficient or unrelated Moonfury argument establishes this effect.
review.implementation: Source-supported full-damage modifier correction candidate. Preserve its separate crit modifier and avoid adding the same direct/periodic bonus twice.
review.code_ready: Apply Improved Moonfire's sourced damage modifiers to the SP-scaled direct and periodic components, without duplicating its separate crit bonus.

items.title: Pet owner-stat inheritance
items.question: Do the wiki's AP, SP, hit, crit, Stamina and armor coefficients hold for Hunter and Warlock pets?
items.current_model: Explicit Forever wiki-derived inheritance is enabled for both families provisionally. The earlier zero-inheritance notes are superseded. Explicit pet talents are additional, not duplicate inheritance.
items.impact: All pet builds; owner gear scaling and pet survivability.

review.answer: Accept the Forever-specific wiki's measured Hunter inheritance as credible working evidence, rather than leaving every listed coefficient as an unanswered question. The older Classic pages do not rebut it. Full owner-hit transfer and extending all coefficients to Warlock demons remain narrower assumptions because the client scaling auras do not export those values.
review.remaining: Warlock-specific power/mana coefficients, full hit-transfer magnitude and dynamic update behavior.
review.implementation: No blanket removal of pet inheritance. Separate answered Hunter coefficients from extrapolated demon coefficients in the register.

tests.requires: Hunter or Warlock pet, one isolated owner-stat change and pet API/damage observations.
tests.measure: Prioritize demon AP/SP/mana and pet update timing; keep owner and external pet buffs distinct. Do not repeat every accepted Hunter coefficient merely because a server script is hidden.

items.title: Pet per-hit damage versus speed
items.question: Do pets of different base speeds deal equal per-hit damage, including AP scaling?
items.current_model: Selected Classic-style pet speeds are retained; the equal-hit model uses the adopted reference-speed treatment rather than normalizing DPS across speeds.
items.impact: Pet choice and Hunter/Warlock melee contribution.

review.answer: The Forever-specific wiki and pet-speed issue agree that different speeds currently retain unnormalized per-hit damage. This is adequate evidence for the present equal-hit convention. It does not settle the owner-AP slope at different speeds or establish that the behavior will remain unchanged at launch.
review.remaining: The AP-added portion of the hit, especially the fixed two-second reference conversion, and future intended normalization.
review.implementation: Retain differing pet speeds and the supported equal-base-hit behavior. Narrow the unknown to AP scaling instead of repeatedly asking whether fast pets exist.

tests.requires: Two same-family/same-level pets of different speeds and two owner AP totals.
tests.measure: Compare the change in pet damage per hit across the AP delta for each speed; control happiness and training. This separates an AP coefficient from the already observed base-speed difference.

items.title: Pet external buffs and action cadence
items.question: Which external buffs reach pets, and how quickly does pet AI spend Focus or mana?
items.current_model: Generic external player buffs are excluded under the adopted common pet model. Focus base regeneration/cap are client-backed; action scheduling is a simulator approximation.
items.impact: Pet damage and resource waste; explicit pet talents remain valid exceptions.

review.answer: The no-external-buffs question is answered for both Hunter and Warlock pets by a direct report and an explicit Not A Bug response explaining the removal of pet buff upkeep. Focus base regeneration/cap are already client-backed. Pet AI scheduling is a separate simulation approximation, not missing evidence that pets need buffs.
review.remaining: Ability scheduling/resource waste, and any explicitly targeted pet-only exceptions.
review.implementation: Close the generic external-buff question. Retain AI cadence as a named model approximation with optional sensitivity checks, not a mandatory repeat of buff eligibility tests.

tests.requires: Only if pet cadence sensitivity proves material; a trained damage ability and a resource trace.
tests.measure: Compare ability use when resource-limited versus resource-capped. Do not mix this with owner inheritance or ordinary spell cooldowns.

items.title: Arcane Shot, Serpent Sting and Volley SP
items.question: What SP coefficients replace the missing client coefficients?
items.current_model: Retains inherited Arcane Shot/Serpent Sting/Volley coefficients. Zero or dummy client fields are not treated as proof of no scaling.
items.impact: SP-heavy Hunter alternatives and AoE; less important for physical-only loadouts.

review.answer: The Forever-specific wiki reports removal of Classic SP scaling from Arcane Shot and Serpent Sting, with RAP scaling instead. This is credible contrary evidence to the retained SP coefficients and should become a source-backed code audit, not stay an undirected coefficient question. The same source explicitly leaves Volley's coefficient undetermined.
review.remaining: Volley's coefficient and a source/code check of the two direct correction candidates.
review.implementation: Check the live Arcane Shot and Sting calculations against the documented RAP terms and removal of SP; retain Volley as an independent question. Do not infer Volley from Sting.

tests.requires: Volley access above level 30, plus independent SP and RAP changes.
tests.measure: Measure each tick under separate SP/RAP deltas, keeping talents and target resistance fixed.

items.title: Auto Shot and special-shot timing
items.question: Does current Forever retain the Classic half-second Auto Shot wind-up and interactions with Aimed/Sniper/Multi-Shot?
items.current_model: Restored original Classic Auto Shot implementation, with sourced special cast times and explicit weapon-cast exceptions. The earlier continuous-autos model is superseded.
items.impact: All ranged Hunter comparisons and haste value.

review.answer: Classic Auto Shot is the explicit reference implementation. The wiki and open beta issues still describe current-beta overlaps and retry behavior, so they do not establish that the reference model exactly reproduces every live beta edge. This is a declared intended-model choice, not a reason to keep a generic mandatory timing experiment on the main list.
review.remaining: Version-specific timing only if the project chooses to emulate the live beta behavior or obtains confirmed intended changes.
review.implementation: Keep the restored reference path and its regressions; do not alternate implementations based on an unresolved sound/retry report.

items.title: Ice Lance coefficient and frozen multiplier
items.question: Is the retained 0.143 SP coefficient correct, and does the frozen multiplier cover the whole hit?
items.current_model: Uses an explicitly assumed 0.143 coefficient and modeled frozen/Fingers interactions; the client damage effect lacks the coefficient.
items.impact: Frost and Arcane–Frost, including comparisons whose baseline casts Ice Lance.

review.answer: The current active talent tree makes Ice Lance available at level 20. The native action's legacy ID and RequiredLevel=60 describe this engine registration, not when a player can first learn the talent. The source still does not settle the assumed SP coefficient.
review.remaining: SP slope and the frozen multiplier's scope. Rank progression remains a separate max-level check.
review.implementation: Move the basic coefficient experiment into the current-beta queue. Do not infer game accessibility from a max-rank-only native registration.

tests.requires: Level-20 Mage with Ice Lance, two SP totals and a rootable controlled target.
tests.measure: Compare noncrit damage slopes while unfrozen and frozen. Keep rank, target level and other talents fixed; distinguish a whole-hit multiplier from base-only damage.

tests.requires: Higher learned ranks if their coefficients differ from the tested rank.
tests.measure: Repeat only the unresolved rank-scaling part, not the entire frozen test.

items.title: Redoubt proc curve
items.question: Does Redoubt proc at 2/4/6/8/10% by rank?
items.current_model: Uses that trait curve and 6% block per point. The curve's proc interpretation is inferred from its top-rank match to the aura data.
items.impact: Protection block uptime and defensive talent value.

review.answer: The active Redoubt definition supplies 6/12/18/24/30 block and a second 2/4/6/8/10 curve, matching the top-rank 10% proc field and the current model. This is sufficient support for the working rank curve, though the second effect's proc interpretation is not independently measured. Redoubt is available at levels 10–14, not only later beta access.
review.remaining: No mandatory test for the adopted source-backed curve; a contradictory current-build observation would reopen proc semantics.
review.implementation: Retain the curve rather than flagging every lower rank as an urgent unknown. Preserve the evidence qualification.

items.title: Inner Focus periodic crit behavior
items.question: Does a permitted periodic spell retain Inner Focus's crit bonus after consumption?
items.current_model: Cost and crit use distinct client masks. Eligible cast-specific behavior is retained; Mind Flay, Death and Starshards do not receive the separate crit bonus merely because they qualify for free cost.
items.impact: Priest alternate DoT/channel priorities.

review.answer: A new public controlled low-crit test reports dynamic Inner Focus crit on existing DoTs while the aura remains active, and loss of the bonus after consumption. This is useful current-beta evidence, but the reporter's preferred snapshot behavior is explicitly an expectation, not a confirmed intended rule. The test is possible now because Inner Focus is a level-20 talent.
review.remaining: Intended charged-DoT handling and current-build confirmation; the small reported tick sample is not a precise coefficient estimate.
review.implementation: Do not silently turn a reported beta exploit into a permanent uncapped DoT-crit strategy. Keep the client crit eligibility mask separate from cost eligibility.

tests.requires: Level-20 Priest with Inner Focus and a DoT in its crit mask.
tests.measure: Compare three arms: no aura, aura activated after the DoT and held, and aura consumed by applying the DoT. Record enough ticks and the exact build; separate live observation from intended design.

items.title: Rogue finisher and poison scaling
items.question: Do the retained AP coefficients and poison proc probabilities match Forever?
items.current_model: Explicit poison base damage is sourced, while several AP shares and 20%/30% proc probabilities retain inherited values. Venom participates in the dynamic periodic model.
items.impact: Rogue build comparisons and poison/physical gear value.

review.answer: A public developer response explicitly supplies base AP ratios of 0.5% for Instant and 0.45% for Deadly Poison, and explains why the ratios are small. Current poisons.go adds no AP term. The missing client coefficients therefore do not establish zero scaling. Instant's direct-hit correction is source-ready; confirm Deadly's per-tick/per-stack placement before applying its ratio.
review.remaining: Deadly coefficient placement and the separate finisher/bleed formulas. Do not bundle all poison and finisher questions into one unresolved test.
review.implementation: Record the missing poison AP support as concrete implementation work. Check client proc-chance records for the base probabilities separately from Improved Poisons and Venom.

tests.requires: Instant Poison access and two known AP totals without changing other damage modifiers.
tests.measure: An optional direct-hit slope check can confirm the published 0.005 term; a rounded tooltip is not a damage sample.

tests.requires: Deadly Poison access and a controlled AP delta.
tests.measure: Measure one-stack ticks and then five-stack ticks to locate the 0.0045 ratio. Audit finishers in separate AP/CP controls rather than mixing poison proc counts with their damage.

items.title: Maelstrom Weapon proc rate
items.question: What determines stack frequency and eligible proc events?
items.current_model: Retains 2 PPM per talent point. The client's 4% per point is a cast-time/cost modifier, not a verified proc chance. Only Lightning Bolt spends the modeled buff.
items.impact: Enhancement damage, resources and weapon-speed value.

review.answer: The latest captured effect chain still separates the per-rank Lightning Bolt cast/cost reduction from proc frequency. No exported PPM record settles the retained 2 PPM per point. The active tree requires 25 prior points: first rank at level 35 and maximum rank at 39, not level 30.
review.remaining: Proc frequency and event eligibility.
review.implementation: Keep the proc model explicit; correct the obsolete level-30 test instruction. Chain Lightning remains outside the captured spender mask.

tests.requires: Level 35+ Enhancement; known rank, weapon speed and extra-attack sources.
tests.measure: Count eligible landed swings/specials and added stacks; compare weapon speeds and talent ranks, recording Windfury separately. Move earlier only if beta access expands beyond 30.

items.title: Instant Maelstrom Lightning Bolt swing reset
items.question: Does a five-stack instant Bolt still reset the next melee swing?
items.current_model: The restored Classic Shaman hook resets next melee to cast completion plus a full swing even at zero cast time. Ordinary hardcasts cannot melee; that does not prove the instant exception.
items.impact: Enhancement APL rankings; all corrected research includes the reset.

review.answer: The restored Classic hook includes an instant-Bolt swing reset, but ordinary hardcast restrictions cannot prove that instant behavior. A five-stack instant test needs maximum Maelstrom rank, reachable at level 39, so this cannot be settled in the announced level-30 beta.
review.remaining: Instant five-stack reset versus partial-stack cast resets.
review.implementation: Keep the modeled reset visible in Enhancement results; do not silently exempt instant Bolt on the strength of a different expansion's rules.

tests.requires: Level-39+ Shaman with five-point Maelstrom and a recorded swing timer.
tests.measure: Cast five-stack Bolt at multiple points in the swing cycle, then compare ordinary and partial-stack casts. Record start, completion and next auto, not only aggregate DPS.

items.title: Two Arcanums of Rapidity
items.question: Do identical copies stack additively or multiplicatively?
items.current_model: Each grants attack speed only; identical copies add. Neither is general Energy haste.
items.impact: Melee/ranged swing rates with two copies.

review.answer: Each Arcanum supplies 1% attack speed, not general Energy haste. The competing two-copy totals are 1.02 and 1.0201: only 0.009804% relative swing-speed difference. Exact stacking is not worth a standing high-effort gameplay test for this benchmark; that numerical bound is not a claim that every possible thresholded rotation has identical DPS.
review.remaining: The exact server stacking law remains unmeasured. Reopen if a stronger stacking effect or demonstrated material timing threshold depends on it.
review.implementation: Retain the additive convention as a negligible-range model choice, not a verified multiplicative-aura rule.

items.title: Healing specializations and utility spellbooks
items.question: Which healing/control-only talents are outside current DPS and tank coverage?
items.current_model: Restoration specializations and much of Priest/Paladin healing are not full supported agents. Utility Tier effects do not invent damage. Individual tank-relevant omissions have their own active entries.
items.impact: Healer simulation and encounters with CC/dispels, not current stationary DPS.

review.answer: Healer-only/CC-only coverage is a product boundary, not an unanswered DPS experiment. Tank-relevant healing, shields and mitigation retain their own active entries.
review.remaining: None for the current supported workload; reopen when a healer or relevant control encounter is added.
review.implementation: Keep in a capabilities backlog, out of the mandatory game-test queue.

items.title: Energy refunds on avoided attacks
items.question: Which builders and finishers refund Energy on miss, dodge or parry, and what fraction of the paid cost returns?
items.current_model: Inherited 80% builder refunds; damaging finishers generally do not refund. Costs are charged before the outcome.
items.impact: Feral and Rogue resource supply, especially before hit cap or when attacking from the front.

review.answer: The captured client distinguishes builders from finishers: Sinister Strike, Claw and Rake have the discount-on-miss attribute bit that Eviscerate, Rupture, Rip and Ferocious Bite lack. This supports the existing distinction, not a universal refund. It does not supply the server's refund percentage. Ferocious Bite first becomes available at 32, not in either announced beta cap.
review.remaining: The paid-cost refund fraction and combo-point retention for each affected family.
review.implementation: Retain the builder/finisher distinction. Compare actual paid cost after talents or Clearcasting, not nominal tooltip cost.

tests.requires: A Rogue with builders/Eviscerate/Rupture, or a level-20 Cat with Claw/Rake/Rip; uncapped Energy and an avoidance-producing target.
tests.measure: Pair resource changes and combo points with each avoided action; subtract independently measured regeneration. Test builders and finishers separately.

tests.requires: Level-32+ Cat with Ferocious Bite.
tests.measure: Separate initial cost, excess-Energy spending, refund and combo-point retention on avoided Bites.

items.title: Spell GCD versus physical GCD
items.question: Which speed effects shorten magical and physical GCDs, and what is the minimum?
items.current_model: The adopted WoWSims-style rule hastes magical GCDs with casting speed, retains fixed physical GCDs, and uses a one-second floor. Missing magical schools were corrected across the audited utility spells.
items.impact: All rotations; especially instant Shaman spells and physical 1.5-second abilities.

review.answer: The consistently applied physical-school versus magical-school rule is a reasonable accepted working model, corroborated by the pinned WoWSims parser. The client gives category 133 and 1500 ms for both shocks and Mortal Strike, so those fields cannot independently prove which GCDs scale. This is not a remaining per-spell implementation hunt.
review.remaining: An optional empirical check of the shared rule and one-second floor; not separate tests for every spell with the same classification.
review.implementation: Keep the adopted rule and its regression coverage. Preserve the distinction between damage school and melee/ranged hit table.

tests.requires: Known casting-speed modifier, one magical instant and one physical 1.5-second action; client cooldown timestamps.
tests.measure: Compare GCD duration independently of cast time. Only test the floor when enough haste is actually available; a 1% modifier cannot establish it.

items.title: Channel speed sources
items.question: Which general-haste effects compress channels, distinct from casting-speed-only effects?
items.current_model: Separate SpellHaste scales supported channels provisionally. Berserking speeds hardcasts but not Arcane Missiles; Missile Barrage has its own explicit tick period. No selected item supplies raw SpellHaste.
items.impact: Mage, Priest and Warlock channels; hypothetical haste scaling.

review.answer: The Berserking/Arcane Missiles observation and separate client attack/cast-speed auras support the current casting-speed versus channel-speed distinction. Current selected equipment has no raw SpellHaste source; the unverified general-haste channel multiplier therefore is not an unexplained benefit currently supplied by gear. This does not establish that every effect called haste behaves identically.
review.remaining: Channel behavior of a specifically identified general-haste source, and extrapolation beyond the observed Berserking case.
review.implementation: Do not merge casting speed into SpellHaste. Keep future raw-rating support under DATA-010.

tests.requires: Arcane Missiles and separately isolated Berserking or Wind Blessed; all missile timestamps.
tests.measure: Compare complete channel duration and tick spacing with a no-modifier control, excluding Missile Barrage.

tests.requires: A concrete obtainable general-haste effect or rating-bearing item.
tests.measure: Identify its aura types before scheduling a gameplay test. Acquisition is not established merely by the hypothetical SpellHaste stat; move to launch only if the chosen source requires it.

items.title: Judgement of Wisdom trigger rules
items.question: Which events trigger Wisdom, at what probability and with what cooldown?
items.current_model: The level-60 return is 59 mana. The inherited event/proc model, including its 50% chance, remains provisional; self-hits are excluded.
items.impact: Mana sustainability of melee Hunters, Paladins and other frequent attackers.

review.answer: The mana amount is sourced: effect 698050 returns 59 at the highest rank. The proc probability is not settled by Wowhead's displayed 50%: all three captured SpellAuraOptions versions instead have 100% on the parent, which triggers dummy intermediate spell 1826. A server filter can exist behind that intermediate. Neither field proves the complete proc rule.
review.remaining: Effective proc chance, avoided-white eligibility, periodic/proc eligibility and ICD.
review.implementation: Keep 50% explicitly provisional; do not replace it with 100% merely from the parent. The current code even allows avoided white swings, which needs its own event-category check.

tests.requires: A level-38+ Paladin with Seal/Judgement of Wisdom, uncapped mana recipients and isolated event sources.
tests.measure: Count mana returns per white hit, avoided white, special, direct spell, periodic tick and triggered effect. Compare event intervals to distinguish chance from ICD; the level-30 cap does not grant this seal.

items.title: Eureka cast and periodic bonuses
items.question: Does the last Eureka charge benefit every tick of the consuming channel/DoT after the aura expires?
items.current_model: The wrapper preserves tagged channel-child bonuses. Ordinary dynamic DoTs are not covered by that wrapper; current resource discounts are 10%, with the engine's additive cost convention.
items.impact: Gnome resource use and damage, particularly channels.

review.answer: Public reports describe already-running DoTs gaining Eureka's bonus dynamically and channels consuming charges per tick; these are unresolved beta reports, not confirmation of the intended charged-cast model. The current client still has explicit direct and periodic damage modifiers. Code preserves tagged channel-child bonuses, but the ordinary dynamic-DoT path is not covered by that wrapper. The older claim that all charged DoTs retain a snapshot is no longer accurate.
review.remaining: Intended versus live-beta charge consumption and periodic bonus lifetime.
review.implementation: Correct the documentation, then reproduce ordinary DoT and channel behavior separately before choosing an engine correction. Current patch costs are 10% for every class, not the old class-specific discounts in the historical racial document.

tests.requires: Current engine, a Gnome DoT caster and a channel caster.
tests.measure: Record tick damage with Eureka before application, after application, and on the last charge. Establish which effects the current wrapper actually preserves.

tests.requires: Gnome Mage/Warlock/Priest with a low-rank DoT or channel; exact build and buff-stack timestamps.
tests.measure: Repeat those three cases in game. Do not infer intended behavior from an open bug report or conflate the old mana-discount amount with current values.

items.title: Read Ley Line regeneration
items.question: Which regeneration components does High Order's active ability increase, and does location matter?
items.current_model: The active regeneration effect is not used; a nearby ley line is not assumed.
items.impact: Potential High Order mana recovery; currently absent rather than a free benefit.

review.answer: Location and duration are answered by the source chain: the ordinary Energized buff lasts 15 seconds; a ley line grants 15 minutes. Both carry +100% mana/power and health regeneration auras. A current public Hunter report explicitly observes mana regeneration in combat, contradicting generic guides that dismiss the racial as purely out-of-combat utility. It does not isolate Spirit versus flat MP5.
review.remaining: Which regeneration components the power-regen aura scales and how casting suppression interacts with it.
review.implementation: The short-duration version is a meaningful missing active even without assuming a nearby ley line. Do not grant the 15-minute version for free, or dismiss the whole racial because location is absent.

tests.requires: High Order mana user; fixed Spirit, a known MP5 item delta, uncapped mana and no other temporary regen.
tests.measure: Compare idle and continuous-spending recovery with the short buff. Record application/expiration and test the long location buff separately if needed.

items.title: Base attributes and class conversions
items.question: Are level-60 naked attributes and attribute-to-crit/resource conversions correct for every supported race/class?
items.current_model: Retained class/race tables with explicit Forever racial changes. Another fork's level-70 attributes were not imported.
items.impact: Every comparison; physical Agility crit versus caster Intellect crit and tank health.

review.answer: Rating conversions are not all unknown: the captured level-60 CombatRatings table supplies 14 crit rating and 10 hit/haste rating per percentage point. Those are distinct from Agility/Intellect conversion slopes and naked race/class base attributes. The latter are still inherited and are not established by the rating file or by low-level character examples.
review.remaining: Level-60 naked attributes, base crit and class-specific attribute slopes.
review.implementation: Do not use equal item budgets or a correct generic-crit import as proof that base stat tables are correct. Avoid importing another fork's level-70 rows.

tests.requires: An authoritative matching-build base-stat/conversion table, if obtainable.
tests.measure: Compare exact level-60 rows and units to engine values; CombatRatings alone does not provide them.

tests.requires: Naked level-60 characters with racial/talent bonuses accounted for, plus isolated Agility/Intellect gear deltas.
tests.measure: Record base attributes, health/mana and crit slopes for each class; race pairs isolate racial offsets.

items.title: Physical multi-school mitigation
items.question: When armor and magic resistance are similar, which mitigation does a physical multi-school spell select?
items.current_model: The inherited threshold approximation acknowledges that choosing the numerically lowest value is insufficient.
items.impact: Conditional multi-school physical effects; not a generic spell-resistance rewrite.

review.answer: The current production spell registrations contain no Physical-plus-magic school combination; the explicit combination found is in a core test. Frostfire's two magic schools are not this case. The unresolved armor-versus-resistance threshold therefore has no demonstrated caller in the current benchmark.
review.remaining: Reopen when an actual supported Physical-plus-magic ability is introduced.
review.implementation: Keep as a conditional engine capability issue, not a required gameplay experiment or a reason to alter single-school mitigation.

items.title: Incoming rage and mitigation
items.question: Does unmitigated damage × 10 / maximum health explain incoming rage at all armor/health values?
items.current_model: That formula is used for Forever Warriors. The low-level doubled low-armor cluster and higher-level behavior remain unexplained; other classes retain their separate rules.
items.impact: Protection rotation, self-damage resource gains and tank stat trade-offs.

review.answer: Public evidence confirms that receiving damage through one's own Priest shield still generates Warrior rage. It does not settle the amount: the incoming-rage issue contains both a damage/conversion-factor hypothesis and a pre-armor/max-health fit with an unexplained low-armor doubling. A developer response says incoming generation is under investigation. These are not interchangeable verified formulas.
review.remaining: Incoming-rage amount, armor/health dependence and high-level extrapolation.
review.implementation: Retain the explicit provisional formula; preserve incoming absorb behavior separately from the PvP rule for attacking someone else's shield.

tests.requires: Nonattacking Warrior, fixed enemy, independent armor and maximum-health changes; no concurrent rage abilities.
tests.measure: Compare uncapped rage per pre-armor and post-armor damage across the reported threshold. Include shielded and unshielded hits without changing the other stats.

tests.requires: Level-60 Warrior and known incoming attacks.
tests.measure: Repeat the selected low-level model at max level before certifying tank resource scaling.

items.title: Berserker Rage's extra incoming rage
items.question: Is the bonus a flat amount, a multiplier, or a damage-dependent rule?
items.current_model: Inherited +2 rage on landed melee/ranged hits and a separate damage-based spell-hit bonus; a proposed 2× rule was not adopted without evidence.
items.impact: Incoming-damage Warrior scenarios and stance/cooldown choices.

review.answer: Spell 18499 states extra incoming rage but its captured effects supply fear/incapacitate immunity, not a numeric rage rule. Its first learned level is 32. Neither a borrowed doubling rule nor the inherited +2/damage-based split is established by that text.
review.remaining: The additional rage rule on melee versus spell damage.
review.implementation: Retain the inherited rule as an explicit assumption; this cannot be a level-30 test.

tests.requires: Level-32+ Warrior, several known incoming hit sizes, fixed armor/health and no outgoing attacks.
tests.measure: Compare rage with and without Berserker Rage separately for melee and spells; distinguish a constant bonus from a multiplier.

items.title: Queued Heroic Strike/Cleave hit table
items.question: Does queueing suppress the off-hand dual-wield miss penalty at level 60?
items.current_model: Attacks remain queued replacements; the penalty is removed only while a queue is active. Low-level observations support the effect, not its full boss-level magnitude.
items.impact: Fury hit requirements, queue timing and resource optimization.

review.answer: The public queued-attack report supports removal of the off-hand dual-wield penalty while Heroic Strike/Cleave is queued, matching the current implementation. That is sufficient to retain the mechanic as a working answer rather than repeatedly asking whether it exists. Its precise boss-level table is part of the broader attack-table question.
review.remaining: Level-63 miss rates and cancel-before-main-hand edge cases, not the basic existence of the observed queue effect.
review.implementation: Keep queue semantics; do not convert these abilities into instant attacks.

tests.requires: Level-20 dual wield, known weapon skill and isolated queued/unqueued periods.
tests.measure: Optional cancellation test: cancel before the main-hand swing and measure only off-hand events occurring inside the queue window.

tests.requires: Level-60 Warrior against a level-63 target.
tests.measure: Include queued off-hand events in CORE-001's table measurement rather than commissioning a duplicate full test.

items.title: Shield attacks and weapon procs
items.question: Can Shield Slam and Shield Bash trigger main-hand effects such as Windfury?
items.current_model: Shield Slam is a main-hand special here; Shield Bash is not registered. Another implementation moved shield attacks off-hand, but its simulations do not prove server eligibility.
items.impact: Protection DPS, rage and threat. Shield Slam requires later access.

review.answer: A competing implementation changing shield proc masks is not evidence of main-hand effect eligibility. The early test and the actual tank damage ability have different access: Shield Bash can be checked now, Shield Slam requires 40, and Windfury Totem requires a level-32 Shaman. A level-20 shield test cannot use Totem as its proc source.
review.remaining: Shield-attack eligibility for specific equipped-weapon effects and Totem.
review.implementation: Do not change Shield Slam's mask without an event-level source. Keep missing Shield Bash registration separate.

tests.requires: Shield Bash, shield and an actually obtainable known weapon proc; autos stopped.
tests.measure: Count proc events following isolated Bashes. This is a partial test, not certification of Shield Slam or Windfury.

tests.requires: Level-40 Shield Slam and access to the exact proc source, including level-32+ Windfury Totem where relevant.
tests.measure: Repeat isolated attacks, separating landed/avoided outcomes and weapon versus shield effects.

items.title: Sunder Armor AP threat coefficient
items.question: What AP-scaled threat was added by the patch beyond the explicit rank threat?
items.current_model: Rank-5 flat threat is 206; no extra AP coefficient is invented from the development-note wording.
items.impact: Protection and Fury Sunder threat, not Sunder armor reduction or direct DPS.

review.answer: The client supplies the patched flat rank threats, including rank-5 206, but retains a zero AP coefficient in the exported threat effect despite development-note wording about AP. No numeric server-script coefficient was found. This uncertainty is about threat, not armor removal or damage, and still matters for tanks.
review.remaining: The effective AP coefficient, if any.
review.implementation: Do not infer a coefficient from the phrase 'small increase'. Preserve the sourced flat values.

tests.requires: Same Sunder rank, stance/talents and enemy; two known AP values and precise threat API readings.
tests.measure: Compare threat slopes over multiple applications, separating first application and refresh. No damage-based proxy is needed.

tests.requires: Rank-5 Sunder if low-rank results establish a nonzero slope.
tests.measure: Verify whether the slope is rank-independent before applying it at level 60.

items.title: Weaponmaster hand-specific armor ignore
items.question: Can an off-hand mace grant the character-wide armor discount, and how does it stack?
items.current_model: The retained equipment gate can grant it from an off-hand mace. The competing upstream main-hand-only rule is not verified.
items.impact: Mixed-weapon Warrior alternatives, not evidence for a free generic armor reduction.

review.answer: The active Weaponmaster tree grants its first point at level 30; the full five-point effect requires 34. The talent text's weapon conditions do not settle whether an off-hand mace grants an owner-wide armor discount. That hand-specific question is genuinely testable in the level-30 beta at one point.
review.remaining: Hand scope and stacking of the mace armor-ignore effect.
review.implementation: Keep the current gate provisional; do not replace it solely with another fork's main-hand-only rule.

tests.requires: One-point Weaponmaster, comparable mace/non-mace weapons, matched AP and controlled target armor.
tests.measure: Move the mace between hands and measure main-hand damage changes; separate the weapon's own damage change and sword extra attacks.

tests.requires: Full talent rank and relevant armor-ignore combinations.
tests.measure: Confirm rank scaling and stacking if the one-point hand test finds an effect.

items.title: Omen of Clarity proc frequency
items.question: Is the client's 100% field a literal proc guarantee after the ten-second ICD?
items.current_model: Direct eligible events grant one free-action charge after the ICD under a provisional literal interpretation; Wrath and resource-free actions do not spend it.
items.impact: Feral and Balance resources, and Bear choices where eligible.

review.answer: The current captured Omen row really does specify a ten-second proc cooldown, 100% chance and no PPM reference, while the description says 'a chance'. That makes the literal implementation transparent, not experimentally established. Search results include stale localized pre-Forever tooltips; those are not evidence for reverting to a Classic melee-only PPM rule.
review.remaining: Effective chance and eligible events after the cooldown.
review.implementation: Keep the explicit provisional interpretation. Consumption exclusions for Wrath/resource-free actions are separately sourced and need not be reopened to test proc frequency.

tests.requires: Level-20 Druid with trained Omen, no other Clearcasting sources and event timestamps.
tests.measure: After each ten-second cooldown, count direct eligible events before the next proc. Compare autos, direct spells and heals; do not count periodic ticks as direct casts.

items.title: Form weapon damage and flat imbues
items.question: Which equipped weapon damage and flat imbue bonuses affect Cat/Bear form attacks?
items.current_model: Retains form-weapon damage rules rather than ordinary equipped-weapon DPS scaling. Another fork preserving an imbue through form changes is not evidence of eligibility.
items.impact: Feral/Bear weapons, stones and damage scaling.

review.answer: The engine explicitly substitutes fixed Cat/Bear weapons and does not use the equipped weapon's ordinary DPS. A disabled block in forms.go is not evidence for adding weapon-DPS-derived AP. No new controlled Forever source establishes flat imbue eligibility in forms.
review.remaining: Form weapon scaling and flat weapon-damage eligibility; separate from proc-enchant eligibility.
review.implementation: Retain the existing form model rather than importing another expansion's Feral AP rule.

tests.requires: Bear and level-20 Cat, matched-stat weapons with substantially different DPS, plus an obtainable flat-damage enchant/imbue.
tests.measure: Compare form attack damage at fixed AP; test the flat effect independently from the weapon swap.

tests.requires: Level-60 forms and high-level weapon effects if low-level results imply scaling.
tests.measure: Verify the actual level-60 base and any effect-specific exceptions before changing synthetic-weapon valuation.

items.title: Bear threat multipliers
items.question: What are Forever's form, Primal Bite, Lacerate and Swipe threat multipliers?
items.current_model: Bear form 1.3×, Primal Bite 1.5×, Lacerate 3.33× and Swipe 2× retain inherited components without complete Forever threat measurements.
items.impact: Tank threat coverage and comparisons; these must not be marketed as verified threat formulas.

review.answer: Current code explicitly traces Primal Bite's 1.5 and Swipe's 2.0 threat multipliers to SoD; Lacerate's 3.33 is also inherited. The public Bear discussions report weak threat but supply no per-action measurements that validate these numbers. 'High threat' in Lacerate's tooltip is not a coefficient.
review.remaining: Separate form and per-action threat amounts, not a single universal Bear multiplier.
review.implementation: Keep the inherited assumptions visible. The newly acknowledged Swipe AP bug is a damage issue, tracked separately from threat.

tests.requires: Bear, white attacks/Swipe, precise threat readings, known damage and no Thorns/proc interference.
tests.measure: First determine the form multiplier from ordinary hits, then Swipe's additional threat; include multiple enemies without duplicating totals.

tests.requires: Primal Bite talent, available from 25.
tests.measure: Isolate direct Bite damage and threat with the previously measured form multiplier.

tests.requires: Lacerate from 42 and eventually level-60 ranks.
tests.measure: Separate application and bleed threat at each stack; distinguish flat threat from damage multipliers.

items.title: Lacerate direct and periodic formula
items.question: Are the stack-dependent weapon term and bleed base the correct Forever damage formula?
items.current_model: 10% form weapon damage per resulting stack and level-dependent bleed base per stack; inherited interpretations remain unvalidated.
items.impact: Bear rotation and damage, distinct from its threat multiplier.

review.answer: The parent rows source 10/12/15 bleed damage per three-second tick, five stacks and a 10% weapon-damage term. The uncertainty is narrower than the whole formula: the description says 'per existing application', whereas the engine uses the resulting stack including the new application. Child 414647 has a separate 20% weapon effect and is not proof of its current script use.
review.remaining: Pre- versus post-application stack count, exact child dispatch and any hidden AP/script term.
review.implementation: Do not automatically double the direct coefficient from an untraced child record. Keep known bleed ranks distinct from the unresolved direct-stack ordering.

tests.requires: Level-42+ Bear, stable AP, no other bleeds, isolated first through fifth applications.
tests.measure: Determine whether the first application deals direct damage and whether subsequent hits use the pre-existing or new stack count; separately measure tick damage and crits.

items.title: Nature's Grace GCD stacking and timing
items.question: Does its explicit GCD reduction stack with cast-speed-based GCD reduction, and when does Wrath trigger it?
items.current_model: Applies both explicit -10% GCD and +10% cast speed; Wrath retains the inherited completion-time proc timing.
items.impact: Balance cast cadence, instant-spell GCD and buff uptime.

review.answer: Both effects are explicit in the current text: increased spellcasting speed and reduced global cooldown. Thus the presence of two modifiers is not itself evidence of accidental duplication. The unresolved part is their composition and Wrath's proc timing. The active talent first becomes reachable at 30.
review.remaining: Composition with ordinary cast-speed GCD scaling and impact versus completion timing.
review.implementation: Keep both sourced components pending the narrow timing test; do not remove one solely because both influence GCD.

tests.requires: Nature's Grace, cooldown timestamps and controllable Wrath travel distance.
tests.measure: Compare GCDs with the aura and an isolated cast-speed control; compare aura activation with cast completion and projectile impact.

items.title: Insect Swarm's final partial tick
items.question: Does the Tier 1 duration extension award a fractional final tick?
items.current_model: Fifteen seconds at a two-second interval yields seven full ticks and one second of remaining aura; no half tick is invented.
items.impact: Balance Tier gain.

review.answer: The source establishes duration and a two-second interval, not a fractional final tick. Seven full ticks over the extended 15-second aura is a reasonable conservative discrete-tick model. Importing retail partial-tick behavior without a Forever source would add damage rather than resolve an observed discrepancy.
review.remaining: Exact final-tick behavior when the relevant Tier 1 bonus is obtainable.
review.implementation: Retain seven full ticks; keep the unresolved edge scoped to this extension, not every ordinary DoT.

tests.requires: The actual Tier 1 duration bonus, not only baseline Insect Swarm.
tests.measure: Capture the final tick and expiration of a full uninterrupted application; check whether a half-strength tick exists.

items.title: Feral stealth openers
items.question: What is needed to support Prowl, Ravage and Pounce?
items.current_model: No opening stealth state or those attacks. Their contribution is absent rather than estimated.
items.impact: Feral opener completeness, especially short fights.

review.answer: This is missing supported spellbook functionality, not an unanswered coefficient for the existing rotation. Prowl is available at 20, but Ravage first at 32 and Pounce at 36. The client specifies stealth/behind requirements, damage effects and combo-point awards.
review.remaining: Implementation of one-time stealth state and supported opener effects; high-level runtime checks.
review.implementation: Add a source-based implementation task, not a level-20 request to demonstrate unavailable attacks. Opener-only contribution does not imply irrelevance.

tests.requires: Current learned ranks/effects and an explicit precombat stealth state.
tests.measure: Implement legal form/position/stealth gates, combo points and one-use opener behavior; ensure normal combat cannot repeat stealth attacks.

tests.requires: Level-32 Ravage and level-36 Pounce.
tests.measure: Confirm opener damage and legal states against the implemented ranks.

items.title: Proc enchants in animal forms
items.question: Can Cat and Bear trigger Crusader, and which weapon speed determines its proc rate?
items.current_model: The generic enchant handler permits form melee attacks and retains a 1-PPM rule. The selected Bear gear and an existing Night Elf Feral profile use Crusader; Forever form eligibility has not been demonstrated.
items.impact: Druid enchant selection, temporary Strength and resulting damage/threat. Simulation confirmation does not establish that the proc occurs in game.

review.answer: Current Crusader eligibility comes from the generic enchant handler, not a Forever form-specific source. It affects selected Bear/Feral equipment, so this cannot be removed as irrelevant. No controlled current Forever evidence found in the reviewed public sources establishes form eligibility or the weapon-speed basis.
review.remaining: Whether forms proc Crusader and the eligible-event/PPM speed basis if they do.
review.implementation: Retain the uncertainty rather than certify the enchant from an inherited Classic/SoD handler.

tests.requires: Only if an enchanted weapon can actually be supplied in the beta; an obtainable enchant is not established by a low character-level requirement.
tests.measure: Compare isolated caster-form and Cat/Bear attacks with proc timestamps and equipped/form weapon speeds.

tests.requires: Crusader access if unavailable in either beta cap.
tests.measure: Repeat the form comparison with enough eligible attacks to distinguish no procs from a low rate. Move earlier if vendors or copied items make the enchant obtainable.

items.title: Bear outgoing and incoming rage formulas
items.question: Does Forever Bear retain damage-based rage or use normalized rules, and how are avoided swings handled?
items.current_model: Bear retains inherited damage-based outgoing and incoming rage. Outgoing miss awards none; dodge/parry use pre-outcome damage. Maul replaces the white swing and does not award ordinary swing rage. Incoming damage is a major resource source in the tank benchmark. Warrior's low-level measurements were not applied to Bear.
items.impact: Bear Maul uptime, other ability throughput, rage from boss damage and gear/talent value. Frequent Maul alone cannot validate the model.

review.answer: Public Bear discussions use 'normalized' inconsistently and do not supply a controlled outgoing/incoming formula. The Warrior measurements cannot establish Bear behavior. The inherited Bear rule is therefore still genuinely unresolved, not a suitable place for a guessed Warrior formula.
review.remaining: Damage dependence, avoidance and incoming armor/health dependence for Bear.
review.implementation: Keep Bear and Warrior models separate until the same controls have been measured for Bear.

tests.requires: Bear, uncapped rage, no Maul/Enrage/Primal Fury and matched attack speed while damage varies.
tests.measure: Separate ordinary hits, crits and avoided swings. For incoming rage stop autos and vary armor independently from maximum health.

tests.requires: Level-60 Bear and known outgoing/incoming attacks.
tests.measure: Check that the low-level formula still fits; test queued Maul separately because it replaces the ordinary white event.

items.title: Overpower/Revenge cooldown and Focused Rage
items.question: Are the earlier independent-timer and undiscounted Demoralizing Shout findings still current?
items.current_model: No. Warrior.Initialize passes one timer to Overpower and Revenge. Demoralizing Shout carries SpellFlagOffensive, so Focused Rage discounts it.
items.impact: The old follow-up report must not create duplicate fixes or false candidate gains.

review.answer: Current registration passes the same timer to Overpower and Revenge. Demoralizing Shout has the offensive flag read by Focused Rage. The old report does not describe a current missing fix.
review.remaining: None for these two implementation claims; missing Shield Bash is separate.
review.implementation: Keep the resolved record rather than repeat the change or schedule a gameplay experiment.

items.title: Shield Bash registration
items.question: Can tanks use the sourced shield interrupt without bypassing Pummel's cooldown category?
items.current_model: Pummel is registered; Shield Bash is absent from Warrior.Initialize. The old report claiming two live independent timers overstated current coverage.
items.impact: Protection interrupt/utility completeness, not damage in a noncasting reference boss.

review.answer: Shield Bash is genuinely absent from Initialize, while Pummel is registered. This is source/code work, not uncertainty about whether the simulated action exists. The interrupt utility is outside a noncasting boss workload, but Shield Bash also has damage, so absence should not be described as automatically zero-DPS impact.
review.remaining: Ranked action implementation, shared cooldown and stance/shield gates; weapon-proc eligibility remains WAR-008.
review.implementation: Implement sourced effects and a shared category with Pummel, without treating a general interrupt gap as permission to guess proc masks.

tests.requires: Current Bash/Pummel rank and cooldown-category records.
tests.measure: Check shield and stance restrictions and both cast orders against the shared timer; compare registered damage independently from interrupt behavior.

items.title: Protection next-swing queue bypass
items.question: Did the Protection APL add Heroic Strike/Cleave damage without replacing a white swing?
items.current_model: Both actions use their queue entries in all ten Protection profiles. An on-next-swing flag rejects direct APL casts of Heroic Strike, Cleave and Maul damage components. Fury and Bear already used the correct queue entries.
items.impact: The old Protection DPS, rage availability and threat were inflated. Earlier selection-gain claims are invalid; current results use corrected inputs.

review.answer: The selected Protection actions use the queue entries, and direct APL invocation of the damage components is rejected. This fixes the demonstrated extra-damage/rage bypass without asserting that every rage formula is correct.
