review.remaining: Historical validation uncertainty is covered by SCEN-016; it does not undo the reproduced queue bug or its structural fix.
review.implementation: Retain the corrected tags and queue guard. Do not reclassify normal queued attacks as a new rage exploit.

items.title: Protection Sunder maintenance starvation
items.question: Does the Protection rotation preserve five Sunder stacks under competing rage demands?
items.current_model: An eight-second refresh window and dynamic-cost rage reserves substantially reduce lapses, with no free external armor debuff. Essential defenses retain priority.
items.impact: In matched coverage samples, five-stack losses fall from 42.22% to 0.57% of single-attacker fights. Mean post-ramp time below five falls from 4.86 to 0.053 seconds.

review.answer: The current APL reserves rage and gives Sunder an eight-second refresh window. The archived observer and reproduced-lapse regression support a substantial reduction in starvation, not an absolute guarantee against every avoidance/resource sequence.
review.remaining: None for the reproduced priority defect. The residual rare lapse is disclosed rather than hidden with an external armor debuff.
review.implementation: Keep the resolved status and the measured, nonzero residual-lapse qualification. This review's resource-threat leads do not justify silently rerunning or relabeling its archived numbers.

items.title: Seal of Righteousness spell-power formula
items.question: Should the proc add SP once or twice, and is the retained two-hand 1.1 factor real in Forever?
items.current_model: Retains the double-add formula and two-hand factor inherited from older testing. A client coefficient alone does not validate the full formula.
items.impact: Both Ret gear archetypes and Protection damage/threat; high-impact scaling uncertainty.

review.answer: The code adds the proc's SP contribution in baseDamage and again through BonusCoefficient; the two-hand factor is explicitly inherited from SoD testing. A current public discussion reports a roughly flat coefficient while using Judgement of the Crusader, but that target-side bonus is not a controlled change in personal SP and the replies disagree. It cannot settle the formula.
review.remaining: Personal-SP coefficient, two-hand modifier and target Holy-bonus treatment.
review.implementation: Do not certify the double addition from the client coefficient alone, or change it using the uncontrolled forum example. This remains a high-value small experiment.

tests.requires: Same low-rank seal, target and recorded weapon speed; two known personal-SP values and one-/two-hand controls.
tests.measure: Measure proc damage slopes without Judgement of the Crusader, then add that target bonus separately. Keep weapon damage, talents and crit outcomes controlled.

items.title: Seal Echo coexistence and consumption
items.question: Can separate Command/Righteousness Echoes coexist, and what exactly spends them?
items.current_model: Separate one-charge Echoes wait for a landed white swing. Avoided swings and melee-classified Judgements do not consume them.
items.impact: Ret seal-weaving damage; the talent itself needs later access.

review.answer: The current Echo aura rows explicitly have one charge and white-melee proc mask 4. That supports the charge count and excludes ordinary Judgements from the consumption family. Separate spell IDs do not prove simultaneous coexistence or what avoided events do. Twist of Light is a level-40 talent, so this is not a level-30 experiment.
review.remaining: Echo coexistence, replacement and avoided-swing consumption.
review.implementation: Retain the sourced one-charge/white-event structure while leaving those script-level details open.

tests.requires: Level-40+ Twist of Light, both relevant seals and aura/event logging.
tests.measure: Replace seals before the next auto, record simultaneous Echo auras, then compare landed and avoided autos plus a Judgement-only control.

items.title: Windfury Totem proc and charge rules
items.question: Which specials/seal procs trigger Totem, how are AP charges spent, and do extra attacks reset ordinary swings?
items.current_model: Separate party buff, exclusive with Grace; not a weapon imbue. Retained ICD, extra-swing timing and seal eligibility remain inherited. There is no second 20% roll to spend a charge.
items.impact: All melee and tank rows; Ret's autoattack gain can exceed the displayed 20% proc chance because specials also trigger swings.

review.answer: The sourced amount and separate Totem-versus-Weapon identity do not answer eligible Seal events, AP-charge consumption or extra-swing timing. The existing matched sim audit explains its output but is not an in-game experiment. Totem is learned at 32; level-30 Windfury Weapon is a different effect and cannot substitute for the test.
review.remaining: Totem proc-event eligibility, ICD, charge use and swing timing.
review.implementation: Preserve the separate air buff and its exclusivity. Treat old matched DPS numbers as an implementation explanation, not a source for the server proc model.

tests.requires: Level-32+ Shaman providing Totem, Paladin recipient, no weapon imbue or other extra-attack source.
tests.measure: Count eligible autos, specials and seal events; record AP aura charges and the next normal swing. Isolate avoided events and exclude immediate recursion before estimating chance.

items.title: Holy melee partial resistance
items.question: Do melee-table Holy strikes and seal damage take partial resists?
items.current_model: Current melee hit/crit handling retains the applicable resistance path; table classification alone does not settle partial resistance.
items.impact: Paladin damage and threat against higher-level targets.

review.answer: Holy school plus a melee hit table is not a physical-school spell, and the current code intentionally retains the resistance path. No controlled Forever report located in this pass demonstrates an exception for Holy Strike or the seal proc. Their resistance treatment cannot be inferred from the melee classification alone.
review.remaining: Partial-resist eligibility, separate from avoidance and crit.
review.implementation: Do not add IgnoreResists simply to improve Paladin damage.

tests.requires: Holy Strike and seal attacks against targets of known equal and higher levels; fixed damage inputs.
tests.measure: Inspect explicit resisted amounts and damage clusters separately from miss/dodge outcomes. A small sample with no resist is not proof of immunity.

items.title: Seal of Fury and its judgement
items.question: What supported Seal of Fury functionality is still missing from Protection?
items.current_model: No Seal of Fury selection, damage proc, judgement, absorb or Improved Seal of Fury mana return. Protection currently uses Righteousness.
items.impact: Major Protection completeness gap; may change gear, rotation, survival and threat.

review.answer: Seal of Fury has current ranked parent, damage, judgement and shield records, including new first ranks 1311649/1311656 at levels 10/18. These are not the obsolete rank-25 alias alone. Parent text explicitly gives a shield-equipped absorb equal to 50% of the Holy damage dealt. The runtime still omits the family.
review.remaining: The implementation and the narrower shield/proc rules in PAL-006.
review.implementation: Treat supported ranks, costs and described shield relationship as source-based work, not a blanket missing-source excuse. Do not import another simulator's entire shield script without qualifying its assumptions.

tests.requires: Current parent/child rank chain and finite-absorb infrastructure.
tests.measure: Implement legal selection, rank/cost mapping, damage, judgement and shield-only absorb; test no-shield and iteration-reset behavior.

tests.requires: Level-10/18 Seal of Fury and a shield.
tests.measure: Validate the implemented low-rank proc damage and absorb relationship; use PAL-006 for replacement/depletion behavior.

items.title: Seal of Fury shield replacement and mana
items.question: Does a new proc replace or add to the shield, and which depletion events restore mana?
items.current_model: Not implemented. A competing simulator's replacement/fully-depleted rule is explicitly provisional, not game evidence.
items.impact: Protection survival and resource sustain; must not grant free mana on expiry or replacement without support.

review.answer: The talent explicitly requires full absorption, gives 15% more mana per attacker level up to three levels, and its triggered text uses player level for the base return. Thus arbitrary expiry or replacement is not described as a mana trigger. Pool replacement versus addition and simultaneous-event ordering remain unsourced. Improved Seal of Fury's first talent point is available at 20, not only later.
review.remaining: Shield replacement/addition, depletion ordering and exact scripted base-return evaluation.
review.implementation: Use the full-absorption requirement as the default implementation contract; separately test unsupported assumptions about pool replacement and prevent reset/expiry refunds.

tests.requires: Level-20 Paladin with the talent, shield, Seal of Fury, known attacker levels and uncapped mana.
tests.measure: Observe successive procs before damage, partial/full depletion, expiry and replacement. Compare equal-level and up-to-three-level-higher attackers; record absorb and mana events separately.

items.title: Hammer of the Righteous availability
items.question: Is the retained spell actually learnable, and what shares its cooldown?
items.current_model: Not enabled merely from a leftover rune/class-skill record.
items.impact: Potential Protection AoE action; absent from current rotations.

review.answer: The known lead remains a retained former-rune record plus another simulator's implementation. The available inventory does not establish a current trainer/talent acquisition path. That is an availability question, not permission to enable the spell and then optimize around it.
review.remaining: Authoritative current learnability and cooldown-category evidence.
review.implementation: Keep disabled until a current acquisition path is shown. Do not ask for a damage experiment before proving access.

tests.requires: Matching-build trainer/taught-spell or live talent evidence for 407632.
tests.measure: Trace the player acquisition path rather than merely finding a class skill row.

tests.requires: Trainer/spellbook UI with unavailable future ranks visible, if the beta exposes them.
tests.measure: Capture an actual offering and requirement. No fixed later test level can be promised until this evidence exists.

items.title: Vindication's target AP reduction
items.question: Does the target-side part of Vindication reduce incoming damage?
items.current_model: Only the Paladin AP gain is implemented. The old comment that enemy AP is never read is no longer true for tank encounters.
items.impact: Tank mitigation and fair talent selection.

review.answer: The active talent and child 440667 explicitly describe target melee/ranged AP reduction as well as owner AP gain. The engine implements only the latter. Target AP is now used by enemy autos, and the tank reference starts at 805 AP, so the old claim that it cannot matter is false. The child is level-scaled; stale rendered rank numbers must not be used as universal constants.
review.remaining: Exact level/rank evaluation and exclusivity with other AP-reduction debuffs before implementation.
review.implementation: Add the target-side effect using the current level formula and strongest-effect rules, with a controlled incoming-damage check. Keep the already-correct 1/2/3% owner AP curves.

tests.requires: Trait curve 82984 and child 440667 level scaling plus existing AP-debuff exclusivity.
tests.measure: Reconcile the rendered level-60 amount with raw level fields; test activation/expiry and competing debuffs against known target AP.

tests.requires: One-point Vindication at 20 and matched enemy swings.
tests.measure: Optional validation of the target aura and damage reduction, without confusing owner AP growth with enemy AP loss.

review.code_ready: Add Vindication's sourced target AP reduction and strongest-effect behavior, preserving the existing owner AP bonus.

items.title: Echo of Justice proc probability
items.question: What is its intended proc probability after the excessive-rate beta fix?
items.current_model: No demonstrated source-supported implementation is enabled for the unsupported effect.
items.impact: Conditional talent/item interactions; not a granted ranking bonus.

review.answer: The traced Justice seal/echo produces a stun; its judgement prevents fleeing. No direct damage effect is present in that chain, and current reference workloads model neither control nor fleeing. Its exact excessive-proc-rate fix therefore is not a required damage/threat benchmark experiment.
review.remaining: Proc probability and control interactions if a stunnable/fleeing encounter is introduced. Such control can affect survival in a different workload.
review.implementation: Keep in the control-capability backlog rather than the current test queue. Do not apply this dismissal to damaging Command/Righteousness Echoes.

items.title: Light's Vigil damage support
items.question: Can the supported enemy-target Holy Shock interaction be represented?
items.current_model: The spell is not implemented; the old healer-only dismissal does not establish that every damage application is irrelevant.
items.impact: Conditional Holy Shock builds and spellbook completeness, not a proven gain for existing Ret.

review.answer: The enemy damage path is explicit: Light's Vigil marks an enemy for the next Holy Shock, makes the consuming Shock trigger no new cooldown and refunds 75% of Vigil's cost. The child damage rows carry a 0.429 SP coefficient. This is a real missing damage ability, not healer-only coverage; its talent and first rank require 40.
review.remaining: Ranked implementation and cooldown/refund interaction tests, not whether an enemy damage branch exists.
review.implementation: Implement the sourced enemy branch and one-active-mark rule before evaluating its DPS; do not infer a whole healer simulation from that addition.

tests.requires: Vigil parent ranks 1310911/1311590/1311595 and their enemy damage children.
tests.measure: Test rank/cost mapping, one active mark, one consumption, refund and Holy Shock cooldown interaction, including target changes.

tests.requires: Level-40+ Light's Vigil and Holy Shock.
tests.measure: Confirm the linked cast sequence and amount at the first available rank; later verify max-rank scaling.

review.code_ready: Implement the sourced enemy-damage branch of Light's Vigil and its one-active-mark rule.

items.title: Protection seal refresh waste
items.question: Does Protection repeatedly pay for an already active Seal of Righteousness?
items.current_model: The unconditional seal filler is removed. Seal maintenance, paid pre-pull buffs and mana-reserved Consecration replace the wasteful rotation in all three ranked Protection profiles.
items.impact: The old five-minute rotation spent about 16,100 unnecessary mana on seal refreshes. The corrected same-gear/talent rotation gains roughly 10–11% single-target DPS.

review.answer: The Protection APL no longer contains the unconditional active-Seal filler. The regression and archived comparisons address a real repeated-cost defect, not an assumption that removing all seal damage is optimal.
review.remaining: Resource-threat accounting remains CORE-014 and older comparison-seed qualification remains SCEN-016.
review.implementation: Keep the maintenance fix; do not restore mana waste merely to reproduce old threat numbers.

items.title: Swift Judgement cooldown timing
items.question: Does Protection actually exploit Swift Judgement’s reset and free cast?
items.current_model: The reset already worked. Explicit APL placement now avoids resetting a nearly completed cooldown and casts the free Judgement before unrelated cooldowns.
items.impact: About 31.5 to 35 Judgements per five minutes; roughly 5–6 DPS from the APL alone with shared support.

review.answer: The cooldown reset already functioned; explicit sequencing now spends the free Judgement promptly rather than resetting an almost-complete cooldown. The same-timestamp regression directly supports that implementation claim.
review.remaining: Historical pooled uncertainty must respect overlapping seed ranges; no new timing-source gap was identified.
review.implementation: Keep the sequencing fix and the SCEN-016 qualification on old comparison statistics.

items.title: Consecrated Ground per-target coverage
items.question: Does the Holy-damage bonus apply only against the first four enemies covered by Consecration?
items.current_model: An owner-wide Holy-damage buff is used instead of tracking the first four affected enemies; this is not a mitigation effect.
items.impact: Can amplify Holy damage against uncovered enemies or beyond the four-target cap. The cap does not distinguish the stationary one-/three-target workloads.

review.answer: The question was misdescribed: Consecrated Ground is not mitigation. Spell 1310905 and active trait 142624 grant 5/10% increased Holy damage against the first four enemies entering Consecration. Code grants a broad owner Holy-damage buff. The cap distinction does not change the stationary one-/three-target reference workloads, but matters with more targets or uncovered enemies.
review.remaining: Target-scoped implementation for broader encounters, not a new mitigation experiment.
review.implementation: Correct the register's question and model description. Track affected enemies for the Holy-damage modifier; do not implement nonexistent damage reduction.

tests.requires: A five-target simulator case plus an uncovered target.
tests.measure: Only the first four covered targets should receive the extra Holy-damage multiplier; one-/three-target in-area cases should remain unchanged.

review.code_ready: Scope Consecrated Ground's Holy-damage bonus to affected enemies instead of granting an owner-wide modifier.

items.title: Retribution Aura provider scaling
items.question: How should the aura use its provider's SP rather than the recipient's?
items.current_model: The retained shared aura lacks the sourced scaling follow-up; stationary DPS receives no retaliation because it is not attacked.
items.impact: Tanks, solo damage and multi-player buff modeling.

review.answer: The public developer response explicitly confirms intended SP scaling for both Thorns and Retribution Aura and says their snapshot bug will be fixed in a later build. The base amount is independently actionable: current rank-5 Ret Aura effect 687971 is 30, while the engine still starts at 20. Thorns already uses its sourced base 22. Zero client SP fields do not refute the acknowledged scripted scaling.
review.remaining: The numeric SP coefficient and external-provider representation; deployment of the dynamic fix.
review.implementation: Ret Aura's base-amount correction is source-ready. Add provider-aware scaling only after sourcing the coefficient; never silently use the recipient's SP for an external buff. Add Thorns to the same follow-up.

tests.requires: Ret Aura's current ranked effect rows.
tests.measure: Add a rank/base-value regression before correcting the 20-to-30 mismatch; preserve Classic separately.

tests.requires: Paladin level 16 or Druid with Thorns, two controlled caster-SP values, distinct recipient and fixed enemy.
tests.measure: Measure the coefficient and swap caster gear after application to distinguish intended dynamic behavior from the known beta snapshot bug. Do not change recipient SP simultaneously.

review.code_ready: Correct rank-5 Retribution Aura's sourced base damage from 20 to 30; provider-aware SP scaling still needs its coefficient.

items.title: Geometry, movement, kills and latency
items.question: Which real fight events are absent from the stationary benchmark?
items.current_model: No terrain/vertical targeting, realistic movement path, encounter add deaths or general player latency. AoE uses target/range approximations; remainingTime is encounter time, not per-target TTK.
items.impact: Consecration placement, cone targeting, grenades, kill procs, stealth/control and short-lived adds.

review.answer: Terrain, movement paths, add deaths and human latency are deliberately absent from the stationary reference workloads. Their exact real-world behavior cannot alter a run containing none of those events. This does not make Consecration damage or current three-target threat irrelevant.
review.remaining: These become requirements for a moving/add-lifetime encounter, not current coefficient tests.
review.implementation: Keep the encounter scope visible and do not interpret encounter remainingTime as measured target TTK.

items.title: Weapon-racial crit and ranged attacks
items.question: Do weapon-specialization racials affect ranged crit, or only melee, spell and inherited pet crit?
items.current_model: A matching held weapon adds MeleeCrit and SpellCrit; the ranged attack path also reads MeleeCrit.
items.impact: Could change Hunter racial comparisons and gear choices without changing generic equipment crit.

review.answer: The Forever Hunter wiki reports that weapon-specialization racial crit applies to melee/spells and the pet, but not ranged attacks. The current helper adds MeleeCrit, which the ranged outcome path also reads, so the engine includes ranged crit. The captured Orc tooltip instead says all spells and abilities; its crit-percent aura does not resolve this live-scope discrepancy by itself.
review.remaining: Whether ranged exclusion is current intended behavior or a beta-specific discrepancy; separate actual crit resolution from character-sheet display.
review.implementation: This is a new source/code conflict, not a reason to change generic equipment crit. A scoped racial correction would need to preserve the melee/spell/pet contributions and matching-weapon condition.

tests.requires: Human or Orc Hunter and matching versus nonmatching melee weapons with equal Agility/crit stats; unchanged ranged weapon and pet.
tests.measure: Record melee, ranged, spell and pet crit APIs before/after the swap, then compare ranged attack outcomes if the display and source descriptions disagree. Check one and two matching weapons separately rather than assuming the bonus stacks.

items.title: Improved Imp's Firebolt damage multiplier
items.question: Does Improved Imp multiply Firebolt's spell-power contribution as well as its base damage?
items.current_model: The talent increases Firebolt's base damage range but leaves the SP contribution outside that multiplier.
items.impact: Undervalues the talent for an active Imp with spell power; this is separate from generic pet inheritance and the undocumented dummy effect.

review.answer: Improved Imp's Firebolt effect is an ordinary damage-percent modifier, with a 10/20/30 rank curve and explicit Firebolt family mask. The engine multiplies only the base damage range, leaving its spell-power component outside the talent bonus. This is independent of the unresolved negative dummy in WL-006.
review.remaining: A focused regression and correction to the full Firebolt damage multiplier; preserve the separate Fire Shield modifier scope.
review.implementation: Apply the documented percentage once to the full Firebolt damage. Current saved Warlock profiles use Succubus or a sacrificed Imp, so this is live-Imp coverage rather than a demonstrated current baseline gain.

tests.requires: Live Imp with zero and nonzero SP at each talent rank.
tests.measure: Check the full damage ratio and ensure the SP component is multiplied exactly once. Do not simultaneously invent a cast-time change.

review.code_ready: Apply Improved Imp's Firebolt damage percentage to the full hit, including its SP contribution.

items.title: Bear Swipe's missing server AP term
items.question: What is Swipe's intended AP coefficient, and has the announced beta script fix shipped?
items.current_model: Swipe has flat base damage and no AP term. A public response identifies a live-beta script guard that also suppressed the intended AP scaling.
items.impact: Could change Bear damage and multi-target threat; copying a remembered SoD coefficient would not establish the Forever value.

review.answer: A public developer response identifies an obsolete SoD guard in the server's Swipe script: current beta Swipe has flat damage, but the intended script adds AP. The response says the guard was fixed internally for a later build and explicitly rejects the claim that it was an SP coefficient. Our Swipe also has no AP term. The response does not give the numeric AP coefficient.
review.remaining: The numeric AP term and confirmation that the announced fix is live.
review.implementation: Track as a newly identified coverage gap, not an already implemented correction. Do not copy a remembered SoD coefficient or silently change current tank results.

tests.requires: A subsequent developer clarification or source-backed updated coefficient.
tests.measure: Check whether the next patch exposes a numeric AP term; absence from SpellEffect does not disprove a server script.

tests.requires: Level-16+ Bear after the announced fix ships, known AP deltas, fixed talent multiplier and target armor.
tests.measure: Measure Swipe damage across AP values, with an SP-only control. Record the build so a still-flat pre-fix result is not mistaken for intended behavior.

stage_definitions.current-beta: An experiment possible at the current level-20 cap, subject to the listed item/ability prerequisites.
stage_definitions.level30: An experiment possible by level 30, not an assertion that the cap has already increased.
stage_definitions.launch: Requires access beyond the announced level-30 beta or max-level content. Reclassify if later beta access is announced.
stage_definitions.offline: Client data, source research, code inspection or simulator testing; no game experiment is required.
